items.statement: Plain words: the village product draws a thorp (handful of farms), hamlet (few dozen homes) or village (few hundred people with church, mill, smithy) always in its landscape; one click gives the township: relief, brook/river with fords and bridges, roads in from neighbours, the village, fields in strips, meadow by water, common pasture, woods at the edge.

Plain words: emulates watabou's Village Generator: density ('crowding') map highest at heart following contours; roads grow as walkers bending along slopes, branching where busy, thinning into tracks; a green (VG look: small square) at the busiest spot; houses along roads/green in plots with garden and paddock; some villages have a palisade built before the roads so roads pass its gates; our rules add parish church+churchyard, manor, mill on water or windmill on rise, smithy and alehouse on through road, wells and pond, outlying farms, open fields in furlongs of strips, meadow on flood ground, woods on poor/shaded slopes; prosperity a smooth gradient (rich sunny dry side, cottagers damp/shaded edge); seven village shapes (VG grown look default, street, green, nucleated crossroads, polyfocal two/three knots, planned row, scatter).

Plain words: palisade stops at river/cliff/gorge/marsh; never fences the village's own water; inside a river bend fences only the neck; trades linked by goods flow (bakehouse near green, smithy where roads meet, charcoal burners at wood edge, alehouses spaced so every end has one); a dossier's 'several blacksmiths' shows that many smithies.

Plain words: editable with the same twelve tools as towns; SettlementForge thorps/hamlets/villages and small towns under 1 500 accepted: every listed institution stands, population exact, listed wall becomes palisade or bank, dossier's word titles the map; growth past 1 500 hands over to the town generator (old village = old core); a declining town shrinks back; default look VG painterly family with ink one click away.

Plain words: everything scales smoothly with head count — no jump at 80 or 400; a 399-person hamlet and 401-person village differ like any two villages two people apart; chances of church, smithy, green rise gradually.

Plain words (item 109): a small place may sit over a cave system or buried ruins (more often in mountains/mines or where SF says ancient ruins, magical node, ley lines); usually sealed, drawn faded for GM; each house over them has a small chance its cellar broke through; well into cave, sinkhole in field, mine into gallery, ruined landmark as entrance; chance of someone digging rises with growth; dwellers (squatters, hermits, cult) only once a way in exists; village church may have a small crypt (most did not); chapel of ease has neither crypt nor churchyard; burial ground is where the town's catacombs may begin after hand-off.

Plain words (item 110): on steep ground houses stand on levelled platforms with low stone retaining walls, steps or cart ramp; crofts and fields follow the slope; a village never generates a viaduct/aqueduct/raised road (only cities) but the user can draw/remove one; one left from a city era stands and loses arches one by one; lanes pass under arches and join only at its two ends; a fishing pier may end in a platform with a net shed; a deserted hillside village leaves grassy terraces.

Every reference behaviour V07 emulates is restated in metres in our own words, cited by file and section, with provenance form 'ref:VG 1.6.9 <behaviour> (code)' whose trace key is row D5 (or P17 for field sectors) of research/findings/code-impact.md §(d) (§17.1 (6), item 62).

Floor and ceiling: population >= 1 and < 1 500 is a village; ceiling = D-33's 1 500 (TOWN floor), ladders meet without gap or overlap; creation request below 1 = F-EDIT conflict whose dry run offers 1 (request) or refused E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE naming the floor (dossier; §7.7 item 15); at an epoch a target below 1 keeps the THORP row and runs §3.12's desertion (never an error; J-V7.2).

Hand-off band (hysteresis; J-V7.68): product is a fold over epochs, never a stored flag (J-V7.3); before first epoch = product that registered Recipe.rung; village passes to base only when epoch target >= 1 500 x (1 + handoff.band) (1 575 at default 5 %); base passes to village only when target < 1 500 x (1 − handoff.band) (1 425); inside band previous product runs on its own rung row at edge (1 560-person village on VILLAGE row, 1 440-person town on TOWN row); no band at creation; alternating 1 480/1 520 never changes product; 1 400/1 600 changes at every epoch.

ProductDecl interface (@plat/layout registry entry, BCR-V7-11; base registers 'base', V07 'village'): id 'base' or 'village'; rungs: Rung[]; stages: StageDecl[]; strategies {network?, enceinte?, fabric?, river?, placement?, fieldSystems?}; phases?: Partial<Record<'siting' or 'growth', string>> (BCR-V7-18); participants?: string[] ('village.plan' afterField order 10 stage VS1 at a village rung; 'village.density' afterField order 20 stage VS2 while a superseded VillagePlan exists under any product (J-V7.67); 'village.pins' afterGrowth order 60 stage VS8 at a village rung (J-V7.126); draws keyed by those stages, table reads VS1/VS2/VS8's (V11 §3.1 row 61; J-V7.122)); rows?: TableId (V6 §2.1 ProductEpochRows; village.json epoch.rows); records?: string (EpochPlacement id; 'village.records' stage S10b; J-V7.125, .129, .130); extraInputs?: Record<stageId, dataKey[]> (village adds 'districts' to S7 so VS5 precedes S7, 'reservations.fair' to S12a); tables: TableId[]; version: string.

Records placement (TV-02; J-V7.125): 'records' names an EpochPlacement (V6 §2.1: place(ctx, record, event), remove?(ctx, record, event)) registered in StrategyRegistry; the dossier step calls place once per record added / count-step member / REPLACEMENT greater placed new (V08 §3.5.1 (c), (d); rebind never offered, TX-06) at an epoch whose product declares it, in binding-key order, before the base's placement (§7.7 One path), and remove after base removal (§7.7 item 2 closeUse); ops commit as single-level batches of the epoch event; 'declined' hands to base placement; on an absorb without an epoch the base's One path placement calls place and §7.7 item 2's removal calls remove, ops in the absorb's commit batches, context = document, tables, product, rung, absorb week (J-V7.128); draws and minted addresses keyed by event.seq (epoch component 0; §3.14; J-V7.129); member and both calls are product registration hooks landing with file f item 202 on M4's grow path (BCR-V7-18; J-V7.132).

Anchor law (DEFINITION §2; J-V7.47): per-rung value = anchor at rung targets 40, 200, 700 people; value at P piecewise linear in ln P between anchors, clamped outside; a cell may state own anchors as a PLaw; weight rows read per entry and renormalised; a count = law value rounded to nearest integer and never below the law at a smaller P (monotone). Every village stage registers a StageDecl with invariants (§3.13 rows), ladder (§3.13), work limits (laws of household count, §6) and budgetMs per village rung (§6); density before network and palisade before roads (PART III items 1, 2) hold because VS4 declares village.density and village.palisadePlan as inputs.

Named draw shapes: u single uniform draw on (0, 1); B3 average of three draws (hump centred 1/2 on [0,1]); F4 = abs(sum of four draws / 2 − 1) on [0,1] crowded toward 0, mean about 0.28; S = 2·B3 − 1 (hump centred 0 on [−1, 1]); each drawn from the named stream the step states.

S0 resolves VillageRequest: given values taken (source recorded); every auto drawn once on blueprint.features from town root (§6.1), after base feature draws (relief, geology), recorded in autoResolved with reason (§5.4), in order: (1) water type from water row; island forces roads isolated; site request's own water (dossier terrain) replaces draw; (2) plan form from forms x cultureForms[culture] renormalised, weights read at P by anchor law; dispersed weight 0 when density dial > formRules.dispersedDialMax (1.4); (3) road topology from roads; nucleated form and district request multiply crossroads by crossroadsWeight (2); dispersed multiplies isolated by isolatedWeight (2); (4) palisade kind from palisade.kinds, present with chance (or denseChance when dial > 1.4) x waterFactor on water map (VG: dry maps only); dossier decides exactly; (5) open space: none for dispersed; green for green form; else present with open.chance[dry/water/island], kind green unless culture latin or greek, a dossier market record exists, or preset VG (then square; J-V7.17); (6) field system from fields x §3.9 factor rows (climate, relief, form, culture, era) renormalised; forest_strip weight 0 unless form row or street; (7) density dial δ = request densityDial else 2^(2 x intent.density − 1) (0.5 -> 1; continuous monotone §7.8) x 1.5 under district, clamped to density.dial; (8) organic = request else true when planned-organic dial >= 0.75; true sets character turn 0. Reference requests map onto these fields by the request-mapping table held with B-VG's baseline rows (BCR-V7-23; J-V7.72).

Bridge-implying record (a dossier record whose kinds row carries implies 'bridge'; today V11's toll_bridge row; V08 §2.6b (3), BCR-V8-32; IN-V07-3) forces a watercourse the through road crosses: when terrain, access, realm cell and draw give none (none or still water) water = brook (on a coastal site estuary at brook width class, exit on sea side); a flowing type keeps its type; unless the realm block fixes the course line, entry and exit bearings drawn on the two frame arcs the through road's two entries divide, so VS4 bridges it (deck may carry the toll house by deckOk); topology with fewer than two entries raised to through unless a dossier access word fixes it (isolated, none). With a fixed word, or on desert without oasis_water, no brook forced: toll house at an entry (else on the heart's approach), toll_bridge_dry reported (J-V7.97).

Territory frame: A_T = max(territory.minKm2, territory.haPerHead x P / territory.usableShare / 100) km2 (700 people -> 20.1 km2) at the request's aspect, plus marginShare of each side as context margin = ladder row's frameAreaKm2AtTarget law with the village floor (BCR-V7-1; frame rule reads it, BCR-V7-30); VG preset replaces it by VG's view at matched.vg.size; frame grows at an epoch by §4.11's rule, never shrinks.

S1 over the territory at village raster sizes; relief primitive follows water type as VG's (ref:VG terrain primitive, D5) mapped onto S1 authored primitives: dry map picks among six equally likely slots (two plains, two hills, a ridge, a valley; hill placed by B3 per axis in frame's middle half; ridge/valley on a straight axis through frame centre at u-drawn bearing); coast a sloping plane to the sea side; pond a hollow near centre; island a mount at centre whose level set is the shore; amplitudes S1 relief-class metres.

Course-first river (J-V7.5; RiverStrategy 'course-first'): (1) width by class brook 2-4 m, stream 4-10 m, river 10-40 m, w = w_lo + (w_hi − w_lo) x B3^2 on water.river; (2) entry/exit on a ring beyond territory edge, entry bearing π·u, exit entry + π(0.5 + u) (90-270 deg apart), axis through a point within 0.3 x territory half-width of centre, Chaikin-cut twice; (3) knots at first cosine extremum and every half wavelength, λ = w x 2^(3.5 + B3^2), pushed along the axis normal by w x (2 or 5, even odds) x sqrt(B3) x cos(2π(s/λ + φ)), φ = u (ref:VG meander spline, D5), plus end knots; (4) interpolating cubic, 8 samples per span, resampled every w/2; (5) confluence adds tributary width w(1 − F4/2) from a source opposite the main chord midpoint turned by ±60 deg x S, meander amplitude decaying linearly to zero at junction; estuary lays the course to a coast on the exit side. S1's carve makes the bed descend monotonically (§4.2 S1 (3); carveMaxCm binding; F-RIVER re-routes); option river 'descent' (base trace) taken when a dossier realm block gives a river course (§3.11).

S2 at village rungs: sequential roster (§10.2) with village class rows; households H = round(P / household.meanSize) split over bands by bandShares (shifted by intent wealth, §4.2 S2); dwellings D_b = round(H_b / (1 + share2_b)); institutions by presence; hinterland demand by farm table village rows (§3.9) under the form's farm mode (BCR-V7-7): grown, street, green, nucleated, polyfocal, row take 'perimeter', dispersed takes 'fill' (J-V7.11). Who lives where (J-V7.54): H_f = min(H, round(arableHaPerCapita x P / fieldHaPerFarmstead) x householdsPerFarmstead) (§4.9 FarmTable village rows); H_o = round(farm.outlyingShare[form] x H_f) taken from farm households' bands in proportion; D_o = ceil(H_o / householdsPerFarmstead); D_v = D − D_o (D after DR7's re-solve with a dossier); §3.8 places D_v, §3.9 (5) places D_o; every household housed once; DR7's residential count D_v + D_o = D. Need propagation unchanged (bakehouse without mill imports flour; watermill demand demands its mill seat).

Government step at village rungs (SR3-01; J-V7.117): at territory-frame rungs S2's government step (§10.2 Government) reads the government row's villageSeat alone (V11 §3.21.1): a dossier government's (DR11) or @seat record's villageSeat class present with >= 1 member (J-V7.104; SR4-09); a request's government forces nothing, feeds only gov presence conditions; reads neither seat class, offices' seat classes nor military share (guard posts per 1 000, barracks) — base rungs' columns (BCR-V7-36 (c)); dossier @office binds to the villageSeat member's building, priest_resident to the parish church (V11 §3.11); guard_post (played by v.watchtower, V11 §3.22) only from a town-watch record or the v.watchtower presence row; no palace, castle, cathedral, courthouse or government-row guildhall placed by the government step (T-V7-13); a dossier record naming one still plays itself by §3.11.

Daylight share (item 102 (a)-(c); J-V7.60): daylight.terrain = sunlit share D(x) over frame and margin at rasters.daylightCm by nine horizon sweeps, one per sun position of g's representative day (path sun at the latitude in force by V08 §2.5's rule, recorded input; equinox; nine azimuths sunrise to sunset), each a single pass in the sun's azimuth order keeping per scan line the running horizon angle; lit when sun elevation exceeds the horizon angle behind; D(x) = lit count / 9 (own algorithm, about 9 x cells operations). Only terrain casts at generation (palisade shade enters VS5 pass 1; V06's building mask the epochs).

Heart (draws on site.centre keyed by town root): a declared heart (request heart, intend or place declaration) is taken; else candidates on the 20 m lattice in the frame's middle half scored by rules.heart: dry and above S1 flood line (hard); slope <= slopeMax (hard; F-V-HEART relaxes); +0.6 within 150 m of a crossing site; +0.5 within 300 m of fresh water (stream, pond or spring cell); +0.3 x (D(x) − mean D); −0.3 x wind exposure; +0.2 x relative height within 300 m (V7C-32); +0.2 x fertile share within 500 m; −0.5 within 300 m of frame; random share 0.15; sheltered shoulder or lee foot of a rise beats both exposed crest and flat bottom (J-V7.34). Polyfocal: k = 2 + (u < polyfocal.extraChance) nuclei by the same score, at least max(spacingMinM, spacingShareRs x R_s) apart; each nucleus after the first carries share 1/k of dwellings for §3.3's radii.

Character (VS1 on village.plan; ref:VG character parameters, D5, 0.7 m per unit): minWidthM = 0.7(8 + 2 B3) (5.6-7.0 m); maxWidthM = 0.7(10 + 4 B3) (7.0-9.8 m); depthRatio = 1.2 + 0.6 B3; branchSpacingM = (minWidthM + maxWidthM)/2 x (4 + 8 B3^1.5) (about 25-100 m); turn = 0.05 + 0.2 F4 (0 when organic). Recorded inputs feeding branch spacing (§3.5), open-space rim (§3.6), District.buildingScale = (minWidthM + maxWidthM)/2 / 7.7 m (VG mean width), and footprint aspect of detached and hovel plans via District.fabricParams.depthRatio (BCR-V7-14).

Settlement radius: A_s = (sum_b D_v,b x toftArea_b + sum_inst plotArea_inst) / settle.settledShare (tofts and crofts at band centres, squalid row for hovels, institutions' plotAreaM2 centre, settled share 0.5); R_s = sqrt(A_s / π): about 100 m at 40 people, 245 m at 200, 480 m at 700 (T-V7-24 recomputes; J-V7.62); street and row stretch along the through road bearing (major stretchMajor x R_s, minor stretchMinor x R_s); polyfocal nucleus R_i = R_s / sqrt(k); recorded.

Mill seat and leat (VS1, when S2 demanded v.watermill): candidates = course points where carved bed falls >= 1 m within 300 m downstream, 150-1 000 m from heart; scored +0.5 downstream of heart, +0.3 within 100 m of a crossing, +0.2 heart side, random 0.1; leat = least-cost channel on VS1's lattice from a take-off upstream where bed >= 1 m above the mill's, to the mill and back below (tail race), at most 300 m, carved in VS1's L0 batch as canal water with one deck where the mill's approach crosses (S1 (5) form); mill plot reserved (Reservation kind institution, owner the mill's institution) in VS1's L1 batch. No site -> F-V-MILL: windmill, else import. Dossier access_to_external_mill suppresses both mills.

S3's non-siting jobs taken over by VS1 (V7C-02; J-V7.50): (a) map border chain on the frame rectangle (§3.2 (9), §2.2 rule 1) laid first in VS1's L1 batch; (b) lattice and edge costs over the frame (§4.2 S3 (3) form) reading village way classes and rules.grade, read by leat, S4's router (neighbour roads, polyfocal joins, row spine) and F-V-TRACK's third rung, each call passing the routed rung so the router prices no raised span (J-V7.90); (c) typed destinations (§4.2 S3 (13) Destination): one per entry bearing (declared, DR3 partners, else S0's drawn), the heart, the mill reservation's attach point, dockable run's densest point where water allows; read by VS4; (d) L0 ponds: village pond (pins.pond 0.4) carved in VS1's L0 batch with the leat at the lowest hollow within pins.pondWithinM (150 m) of heart, site on hinterland.decor keyed by heart; centrepiece pond and fishponds sited after L0, uncarved.

VS2 density raster: box = square around heart of half-side max(1.6 R_major, 150 m) clipped to frame, at densityCm (4 m): about 385 x 385 cells at VILLAGE target, 195 x 195 HAMLET, 80 x 80 at a 40-person thorp (300 m floor square 75 x 75 below about 30 people). Reference height (ref:VG density elevation band, D5, re-anchored on heart): c = heart + polar(0.5 R_s S, π u) on village.density; h_c its ground height or, in water, the highest shore height within 2 R_s; Δh = height range. Per cell: q = clamp(1 − 2 abs(h_c − h(x)) / max(Δh, bandMinM), 0, 1); r = radialPeak (1 − ρ/(reachShare R_s)) (ρ distance to nearest nucleus, anisotropic for street and row); w = waterTerm max(0, 1 − d_water/waterReachM); s = sunTerm (D(x) − mean D); g = slopeTerm max(0, slope − slopeFrom)/slopeFrom; f = floodTerm [below flood line]; n = epsShare fbm3(x/120 m); density = smoothstep(clamp(δ (q + r + w + s + g + f + n − 1), 0, 1)), 0 in water. VG preset: w, s, g, f, n = 0, ρ from map centre, reach = map half-width. Heart reaches smoothstep(min(1, 1.5 δ)): 1 by default, about 0.84 at sparse end.

Density bands: FieldBands field 'density', cuts [populated, 0.35, 0.7], bands empty/scattered/close/dense, source 'table' (§4.5 field type); read by VS3 keep test, VS4 (road -> track below populated; branch spacing), VS6 and S10a slot weights, §3.9 orchard chance, spotlight, item 101 density brush (T8 fill) whose strokes composite (§7.2); not stored at full resolution, recomputed from recorded inputs on load (§2.9).

VS3 palisade (only when S0 resolved one or a dossier lists a wall record; VG construction D5.5; PART III item 2): EnceinteStrategy.trace binding (§4.12; J-V7.77): boundary = density box; gateSites = [] (gates are VS4's); reservations = mill reservation; terrain, water as given; policy {waterfront 'open', placement 'aroundAll'}; density read via declared input village.density; result = planned trace committed by VS4. Steps: (1) 10 x 10 lattice over the box (step about 0.32 R_s), each point offset within its cell by (0.1 + 0.8 B3) x step on both axes, survives with chance density(p) − keepBelow on village.palisade keyed by lattice index; (2) convex hull of kept points, flattest vertex dropped while 2 x area / (distance between neighbours)^2 < flatten (0.1); (3) closed interpolating cubic at 12 samples per span, resampled every resampleM (17 m), last point dropped within half a step of the first; (4) defensible ground (our extension, weight 0 under VG): each vertex pulled up to 10 m toward highest ground in its normal band (base S5a pull in miniature), order kept.

Barrier closure at village scale (item 106 (a), (b); off under VG whose rule is the water cut alone: stretches in water or within bandM of a shore cut, open chains closure 'shore'): (a) barriers = every shore (sea, lake, pond, river, brook alike; village never fences its own water, J-V7.26), bank segments of kind cliff and marsh (§2.3), terrain runs steeper than the defensibility table's cliff threshold (V11's item 106 (a) rows), gorge features; (b) reach = min(wall.barrierReachM, barrierReachShare x R_s) (base 150 m cap at VILLAGE target, about 120 m HAMLET, 50 m at 40-person thorp); each maximal run of trace vertices whose outward normal meets a barrier within reach replaced by connector to nearest barrier point, barrier edge, connector back (river bend fenced across its neck; scarp or marsh fenced on approachable side only); spare ground inside enclosure and perimeter; VS6 marks faces outside the pre-reach trace as reached (no frontage runs); S10 toft strategy lays one commons-owned close per reached face split at 1 ha; S12b types yard parts paddock/orchard/garden by suitability (item 106 (b) intramural gardens); reached ground excluded from S10a quotas and VS6 capacity check; VS5's 2 ha interior cut never applies (J-V7.75); (c) arcs classified by defensibility table: water arcs, arcs within bandM of shore, sheer cliff, gorge CLOSE (no wall); steep slope and deep marsh LIGHT; open ground FULL; a non-water closing arc shorter than minStretchM between two walled stretches walled through; water arc never walled; (d) anchors: walled stretch ends anchor on barriers (base shore, bank, cliff anchor kinds, §2.7) with end post for palisade and earthwork, small tower for inner (BCR-V7-20); closure 'barrier' when any arc closes, else 'ring'.

Kind and section by stretch (item 106 (c)): full stretches take the kind's section — palisade timber stakes 300 cm high, 40 cm thick; earthwork a bank 4 m wide, 180 cm high with a ditch 3 m wide outside; inner a small stone circuit 500 cm, 120 cm thick, material stone (the one masonry enceinte of a village, J-V7.15); light stretches take lightHeightCm: wattle fence or dead hedge 150 cm on palisade, low bank 100 cm without ditch on earthwork, parapet 250 cm on stone; closing arcs carry nothing; band bandM (8.5 m) each side of every walled stretch is the no-build band every later stage reads.

Planned then committed: trace data village.palisadePlan read by every tracker at every step; VS4 commits with the network in one L1 batch as an Enceinte of stage 1 (placement aroundAll, waterfront open at every village rung, §3.11 DR2), gates = crossings VS4 made, split at them; a walled stretch touching no gate kept by default (J-V7.27), dropped under VG; S7 builds furniture (§4.8): gatehouse across each through-class gate, timber gate elsewhere, anchor furniture at every barrier anchor. Failures: fewer than three kept points or trace holding no nucleus -> F-V-PAL; walled stretch end with no barrier to anchor -> F-V-ANCHOR; no gate after VS4 -> F-V-GATE; never a map rebuild.

VS4 tracker network (NetworkStrategy 'tracker', §4.12; VG D5.6; PART III item 3): reads density raster, planned palisade, mill reservation, S1 crossing sites, VS1 destinations and lattice, S2 dwelling count via declared inputs; enceintes carries planned palisade; tracker transient {lineage, class through/road/track, pos, heading, target?, water repel/attract, length, limit}, never a record; ways are records. Terrain vectors from S1 height raster (bilinear gradient), n unit normal, n_h level component, n_z upright: uphill/downhill = −/+ n_h x n_z^2 (weakened on steep ground); two contour directions n_h rotated ±90 deg at full length; best-aligned of four with heading = terrain vector t.

One tracker step (stepM 3.5 m, round-robin in lineage order): (1) leaving the frame stops (open crossing cancelled; through road's end becomes an entries row through/neighbour/dead_end); (2) water ahead: an S1 (5) crossing site whose deck lies within bridgeSnapM (30 m) of the heading is taken (next points = deck ends, Bridge becomes built, continue from far end, water repel); else on a brook or stream (width below S1's ford row) through or road lays a ford perpendicular to flow; track fords brooks only; else a through tracker sites a deck by F-ROUTE's extra-bridge rung (§5.2) perpendicular to flow, ground-part-0 deck by S1 (5) rules, never raised; a road does so only when far bank density >= populated and no deck within crossing.minSpacing, else stops and records a Landing; sea, lake, pond never crossed: through tracker steers along shore at most shoreSteerSteps (20) then F-V-TRACK; others stop and record a landing; (3) wall: closing arc is no wall (crossed freely); a walled stretch: through always makes a gate; road only when crossing lies >= max(perimeter / 6, π/2 x branchSpacingM) along trace from every gate so far, else stops (VG rule); track stops; (4) merge: a laid or pending way point on ground part 0 within lookAheadM ahead (own last four steps excepted) -> attracted onto that way (§3.6 attraction), previous vertex smoothed, T junction, stop; of a raised way only its two feet are merge points; supports obstacles, spans passed beneath (§3.5a (3)).

Tracker steer and density: (5) v = t x weight[class] + water + pull + push; weight through 0.5, road 1, track 2; water = repulsion vector of every water cell within waterReachM (inverse-distance sum normalised by disc area) x waterRepel or waterAttract by mode, applied only while heading toward water; pull: pullThrough x sqrt(d / frameSide) for through road, pullRoad x d / frameMax for a road with a target; push = wallPush along trace normal in direction of travel inside the palisade band; a road applies v only when its component across heading exceeds turn; through and track always apply; grade guard (our extension, off under VG): when grade along new heading exceeds maxGrade[class] (through 10 %, road 14 %, track 20 %), heading turns toward nearer contour vector until within grade or 60 deg turned. (6) road below populated stops and a track continues (lineage .../t); road with no junction within branchSpacingM / max(density, 0.05) branches and stops: left only, both, right only a third each; continuation 0.9 after one side, 0.1 after two (village.track keyed by branch lineage); each new tracker a road with parent's opposite water mode; a track stops when length passes limit branchSpacingM / max(F4, 0.05) (never below branchSpacingM); a track end outside populated area = an approach (outlying farmstead drive); after a bridge mode is repel.

Seeding order: (1) through roads by topology: isolated none; through one from the entry at the entry bearing (VS1 destinations order: declared bearing, dossier partner bearing, else π u stretched by aspect) toward the opposite side, target opposite frame point or second partner's destination; dead_end one from heart's populated point out to entry; crossroads a through road plus at its dry point nearest heart one or two perpendicular through branches (second along a second partner's bearing); (2) open space (§3.6) before side roads; (3) side roads of the through road: interior vertices in shuffled order (village.track), each dry, above populated, outside the open space, no junction within branchSpacingM / density, branch perpendicular; (4) gates at every crossing of the through road with the planned palisade; (5) wharf, its road and piers (§3.10; J-V7.51) when water has a dockable shore, else a single pier at each recorded Landing with no bridge nearby; (6) isolated start when no tracker exists: open space at heart if it fits, else two opposite roads along one of four terrain vectors plus each perpendicular with probability density/2; (7) neighbour roads (0 under VG): neighbourTracks roads at neighbour destinations (dossier partners' bearings or drawn bearings >= 45 deg from every through road), routed by S4's router (§4.3) over VS1 lattice from frame inward until meeting the network, road class inside perimeter, track beyond; (8) rounds until no tracker live or work limit (§6) reached (F-V-TRACK); before finish raised way feet joined (§3.5a (3)); (9) finish: a branch with exactly one road and no continuation has its corner cut; palisade split at gates; gateless stretches kept (dropped under VG); empty-road prune (vg.emptyRoadPrune; on under VG, off by default, J-V7.74): under VG a way whose frontage lies wholly below populated and reaching no entry, landing, approach or open space removed.

Rung gate on the router (item 110 (b) revised ~23:40; J-V7.90): every call a village stage makes to S4's router (neighbour roads, polyfocal joins, row spine, F-V-TRACK third rung, raised way stub track) and F-ROUTE's extra-bridge rung pass the routed rung; the router's raised-way gate is closed at THORP, HAMLET, VILLAGE: no span priced, no raised part laid whatever the drop; water crossing = part-0 deck by S1 (5); dry ravine detoured by router costs and grade guard; the gate is the owner's rule (provenance owner), no village.json cell, cannot be moved by editTable or calibration; village registers no raised-way generation source (T-V7-46; BCR-V7-33).

Plan forms (J-V7.6): street — through road is the spine; side-road spacing x streetSideSpacing (3) within major radius; per side, with probability streetBackLane (0.5), a back lane parallel at toft-plus-croft depth (spine offset and smoothed, joined at both ends by short lanes); green — open space is a long green and the through road divides along its two long sides as rim ways (houses face the green); nucleated — through becomes crossroads with probability nucleatedCrossroads (0.6); branch spacing x0.7 within 0.6 R_s; polyfocal — each nucleus its own isolated start; nuclei joined by S4-router roads between open spaces or starts; through road passes the nucleus nearest its line; row — turn 0; spine laid by S4's router over VS1 lattice with straightness weight rowStraightness (5) along contour through heart; no branching within the row; back lanes both sides with probability rowBackLane (0.8); equal slots; dispersed — no open space; branch spacing x dispersedBranch (1.5); track limits x dispersedTrackLimit (2); farm households at approach farmsteads.

VS4 output one L1 batch with the palisade trace and open spaces: ways through (7 m), secondary (village street, 5 m), lane (back and joining lanes, 3.5 m), track (3 m, surface dirt), ford, bridge, quay, pier (chief pier with its head where drawn); junctions T, X, Y, end, gate, bridgehead, square; plan entries and approaches; village.landings. Widths are the village rows of §4.3's width table (BCR-V7-25; own, calibratable; VG's roads 5.6-7 m).

Raised way on a village map (item 110 (b) revised ~23:40; J-V7.83): a village never generates one (rung gate), a user may add one at any rung, and one generated in a city epoch stays when the place falls below the hand-off band (V06: a fall below CITY never removes one); village stages lay ways, plots, fields around it on every derivation and epoch. (1) Sources at village rungs exactly two: a declaration (T4 road with raised, the aqueduct class, or the skeleton file line) and a way carried down through the hand-off from a CITY epoch; no village stage or phase creates one. (2) Data key raised (RaisedRead) published by the declaration layer; VS3, VS4, VS5, VS6, S10, S12a, hinterland unit, VS8 declare it; no village stage writes a part from 1.

VS4 around a raised way: merging on part 0 only (merge test and router read part-0 ways; only its two feet may be merged onto); supports are obstacles: footprint grown by raised.supportClearM (1 m), in a uniform grid index of supports (cell 10 m); a step entering one turns by turnStepCdeg (15 deg) steps, first to the side nearer the target else higher density, alternating, up to turnMaxCdeg (60 deg) either way, failing that F-V-TRACK's first rung; under a span (standing, ruined or cleared) passes freely (no junction, crossing record, gate or stop); feet: after rounds and before finish, at every derivation, each foot joins the nearest part-0 way vertex within endSnapM (20 m) as a T junction (vertex attracted by §3.6 attraction); no vertex in reach: stub track routed by S4's router (rung gate closed) to nearest way, lineage way:raised/<raised way>/foot<0 or 1>, reported W_RAMP_STUB; failing that F-V-FOOT; joins and stubs in VS4's L1 batch; no frontage: a raised way incl. ramps carries no frontage run and is never measured from by VS5's interior cut.

VS3: a support in the planned palisade band is taken into the stretch (abuts its two faces), never moved, never a gate; a gate within supportClearM of it moves along the trace to the nearest clear point; trace passes beneath a span as an ordinary stretch; a raised way crossing the circuit makes no gate; barrier closure never treats a raised way as a barrier. VS5/VS6/S10: under-deck strip = deck footprint grown by stripClearM (2 m) holds no toft yard part and no building; S10's toft strategy lays a frontage slot whose toft meets the strip as a close (paddock, orchard, garden; joined to or held by nearest built dwelling's household), never raced; VS6's capacity estimate subtracts those slots before F-V-SLOT; S10a quotas over raceable slots only so D_v stays exact; crofts, closes, paddocks may pass beneath with supports cut as holes (§3.6 hole rule); perimeter unchanged. S12a and hinterland: field, meadow, common, pasture, wood faces pass beneath with supports as holes; furlong strips run through; no hedge, headland or field line follows a deck; §3.9's claim and suitability ignore the deck.

(7) Spans: V04's arch-vault source registered at every village rung (§3.16 (1); C4-110-3); V04's span rule decides open or vaulted, with one condition asked of V04 (dependency (5)): a span over a hinterland face (field, meadow, common, pasture, wood) stays open at every rung; inside the perimeter a vault is storage by V04's chamber row, holds an institution only by declaration; street-vault and bridge-vault sources keep their TOWN gate. (8) Aqueduct at a village: terminal a fountain Pin or basin as declared (basin default; V1C-85); cistern only by declaration (V04 terminal cistern, C4-110-6); VS8 well coverage counts each delivery point of an aqueduct with unbroken channel as a well (no well within pins.wellWithinM 120 m); when a span is ruined or cleared in the engine's decline (V6 §3.19.2) channel broken, points stop counting, coverage sites wells at next derivation or epoch. (9) A raised way is never an end anchor (crossing reads part-0 bridges and fords only; V1 I110R-4); name tags and plate water qualifier read part-0 crossings only; its label is the base way label and V07 §5.3's landmark word.

Adding and removing are local (V07 §4.3): adding (T4 with raised, or aqueduct class): the declaration's commit joins feet by the base's rule, VS4 re-joins at every later derivation; dry run re-races blocks whose raceable slots the strip removes, each keeping its recorded quota; a block that can no longer hold its quota passes the shortfall to neighbouring blocks (sharing a frontage way) by largest remainder on their free slots' density, failing that F-V-SLOT's rungs (D_v stays exact); re-cuts hinterland faces with support holes; count badge (item 101 R14) 'the arches pass over 6 tofts; 4 houses move within their blocks'. Removal: V09's delete of a declared way (declaration inverse) or for a carried generated way C6-39's suppression (reason key in log), dry run 'the town will not rebuild this aqueduct; undo brings it back'; strip slots return to the race, faces re-cut, V04's vaults under it go in the same commit (C4-110-3). (11) Every rule above is draw-free (pure functions of raised and recorded inputs): with no raised part every village stage's output byte-identical to the build without §3.5a (T-V7-46, T-V7-52), with one the same on every engine.

Open space (during VS4 step 2; J-V7.17; draws on village.open keyed by nucleus ordinal): (1) size (VG D5.7): rim holds n of the widest ordinary dwellings, n uniform in open.rim (12-19), circumference n x maxWidthM, r = n x maxWidthM / 2π (about 13-30 m) x clamp(sqrt(P / target), open.scale); (2) centre: populated point from the nucleus outward along a spiral of random angles whose radius grows x1.1 per step from half a cell, skipping water, the densest point seen before density first falls below populated; a through road within 2r moves the space to its densest dry vertex with its tangent as orientation; (3) shape: square round with probability open.round (0.7 dry / 0.9 water) as regular polygon of one vertex per about 3.5 m, randomly turned, else a square of side 2r resampled every 3.5 m; green a rounded lens W wide and W x lengthRatio long, W in widthM, area >= haPerThousand x P / 1 000 ha, long axis along through road (probability 0.7) or across; both stretched along contour by 2^min(1, slope / 0.25) and turned to contour direction or road tangent.

Open space records: green = Reservation kind green (BCR-V7-5; owner commons) with Greenery kind green; square = plaza reservation. With a market in S2's manifest (a dossier market record: class of V11's market profile family, V11 §3.4: at village-reaching tiers market (weekly_market, market_square, periodic_market), market_hall (fish_market), fair_ground (annual_fair), slave_market; or custom archetype mercantile-market), else the market law rules.market.law (900, 0) -> (1 300, 0.2) (one uniform draw on village.open keyed by the first nucleus's ordinal and 'market', compared with the law at the population, same draw at every epoch): the open space (first nucleus's) carries the principal market rank (§4.2 S3 (12) rule with the plaza candidate alone; J-V7.17); with no open space the market is a flanking square astride the through road at the heart ('widened street'); that reservation is what dist.market measures to (BCR-V7-36 (b); J-V7.111).

Market halls' claims (SR2-03; J-V7.112): a market-hall-family class playing itself at a village rung with a nearMarket row (today V11's market_hall for a fish_market record; SR3-06) has no S3 claim, so VS4 makes it on the reservation carrying the market: A_h = family footprint p50 / claimArea.marketHall.coverage (0.8) at the band of the median household in bandShares; reservation polygon first scaled about its centre by sqrt((A + sum A_h) / A) (A its area after step 3) so open ground left is step 1's size; (7)'s checks on the grown space; each claim cut inside against its rim: rectangle of area A_h, depth min(sqrt(A_h / aspect), depthShareR x r) (r grown space radius, green half-width W/2, flanking square half-side), long side along the rim, centred on the rim vertex nearest where the through road meets the space (second hall at the rim vertex farthest from the first); Reservation kind institution owned by the member (§4.2 S3 claim form), laid in VS4's L1 batch; S10 lays it as the hall's plot, S10b seats it claims-first so nearMarket 60 hard holds and no toft slot taken. Any other market-hall-family class playing itself (V11's slave_market, pulled toward harbour or gate) takes no claim: S10b seats it claims-first on adjacent slots joined up to A_h by S10 (7)'s join law, sited by own rows, as a cloister-family class joins slots (SR3-06).

Fair field (SR2-02; J-V7.111): a fair_ground member (dossier annual_fair; V11 row: market reservation, secondary, extramural, no building) laid by VS5 after the perimeter in its L1 batch: rectangle of market.fairHa (1.5 ha), side ratio fairAspect (2), long side along the through road just outside the perimeter at the through road's perimeter crossing nearest the heart (a neighbour road's where no through road), on the side with lower mean slope, clear of water, mill reservation, a raised way's strip and supports, and the frame margin; Reservation kind market, rank secondary, owner commons (output reservations.fair); member binds to it (builds nothing); between fairs common grazing: S12a claims its face as a common face before the outward claim (§3.9 (4)); never what dist.market measures to; where it cannot be laid F-V-FAIR; at a village epoch the same placement runs in village.records (record) and step (m) (roster member).

(5) Centrepiece (VS8 places it; decided here): none when the shape meets water; else from open.centrepiece (well, large tree, pond — 'a small decoration pond inside the green, the village pond' — cross, nothing); under VG a tower with probability 0.1 (round) or 0.5 (square): a real building, triple height, footprint maxWidthM x (1 + F4) x depthRatio on a side; else a tree or well at even odds. (6) Roads from the rim: rim vertices shuffled, each dry with no junction within branchSpacingM x min(1, perimeter / (5 x branchSpacingM)) / density, start an outward road along the rim normal. (7) Checks: space inside the planned palisade and clear of water and mill reservation, else F-V-OPEN.

VS5 (after VS4, before S7; V7C-03): (1) perimeter = region where density >= populated, closed by a 20 m morphological close, Chaikin-smoothed, united with the palisade's enclosure, open spaces and mill reservation, clipped to frame; deep interiors cut out (J-V7.53): in each network face inside it, the part farther than the modest band's toft-plus-croft centre depth (toftM + croftM, 95 m) from every frontage-carrying way (through, secondary, lane, a track inside the region, on ground part 0, never a raised way) is an interior; an interior > slot.backCloseHa (2 ha) is removed (hinterland face from the start, J-V7.19; a hole by §3.6 hole rule); interiors of reached ground never cut; result inserted as L1 chains with role perimeter by same-level splits (§3.3). (2) District: faces inside form one District of kind village (PART III item 4; BCR-V7-4), one quarter, fabric 'village-ways', buildingScale and fabricParams.depthRatio from the character; faces outside are the hinterland pseudo-district's (§4.9); a polyfocal second nucleus is inside the same district (ends name it); containment building in plot in block in district holds (§5.3). (3) Prosperity pass 1: §4.5 field over district and margin at 32 m cells with village driver rows (own, calibratable): heart and open space (+), through road frontage (+), high dry ground (+), damp and flood ground (−), palisade lee (base wall driver at 0.3 of its weight), item 102's daylight term (terrain and palisade casting, one pass, never iterated); FieldBands follow §4.5 rule from bandShares (capacity and demand agree by construction); pass 2 is S10a's (institution kernels: church and manor up, smithy and tannery down).

VS6 village-ways fabric (FabricStrategy 'village-ways', PART III item 3): no block cut, every district face is a block; frontage runs along each side of every through, secondary and lane way on ground part 0 facing into the district, along track ways inside the perimeter at half weight, and outward along the open space's rim; run starts clear of the junction at the way's half-width + 4 m + minWidthM x B3 (VG D5.8); a block face deeper than twice the band's toft-plus-croft depth keeps its interior beyond the crofts as a back close (commons-owned close, at most backCloseHa 2 ha); VS6 marks reached faces (no frontage runs).

VS6 capacity check and top-up (moved from S10a so no L1 write follows S9; J-V7.52): slot estimate per run = length / frontage centre of its band at prosperity pass 1; institutions' slots = sum of templates' plotAreaM2 (claim-sized family from rules.claimArea, a rim-claimed hall counting 0) / modest slot area; when estimate < D_v plus institutions' slots, F-V-SLOT's first three rungs here: band-minimum widths (recorded for S10), track frontage at full weight, then up to fail.slotTopUp (3) top-up road trackers from densest perimeter junctions grown by VS4's step rules inward only (stopped at perimeter chain), committed as VS6's second L1 batch with their frontage runs; reached ground counts toward neither side; slots whose toft meets a raised way's under-deck strip subtracted.

Slots (S10, PlotStrategy 'toft'): widths from band's toft.frontageM at the run's prosperity, jittered by toft.jitterCv (0.05 in row village); slots abut; depth toftM + croftM at its band, clipped by the block's per-frontage region (§4.7 S10), rear line on the region's median where two frontages share a block; each slot cut perpendicular into one plot with two yard parts, toft (house yard, toftM deep) and croft (garden-close behind), plus a drive part where §2.4's row asks. Under VG the slot is VG's house rectangle: width uniform in [minWidthM, maxWidthM] (a large one maxWidthM x (1 + 3 F4) with probability 0.15/k, k = 3 plus large houses already laid), depth width x (1 + 2(depthRatio − 1) u), set back offset x (1 + F4) (offset 7 m on through road, 5.6 m elsewhere), advancing by width + minWidthM x B3 built or not, driveway with probability ((width − minWidthM)/(maxWidthM − minWidthM))^2, no croft (VG D5).

Block quotas (S10a): D_v and the institutions allocated to blocks (reached faces excluded) in proportion to sum over raceable slots of density(slot midpoint) x m (slots under a raised way's strip and deck plots excluded), m = 2 on the open space's rim else 1 (VG multipliers), by largest remainder, ties by block address, recorded in each block's Allocation; re-selecting one block never moves another's count (§6.3; J-V7.8).

Slot race (S10b): institutions first, claims-first (§4.7 S10b): each class placed by the one solver with its §2.4 row (profile, relation rows, coverage, supply links, spacing), joining adjacent slots up to template plot area (S10 (7) join law); a 'the claim's' plot family reads rules.claimArea (cloister joins slots up to band's claimArea.cloister; market-hall with nearMarket takes its rim claim and no slot; other market-hall (slave_market) joins slots up to A_h sited by own rows; SR3-06); order = item 105 (f)'s at village rungs: dossier and author claims; anchors (mill seat reservation, open space, entries, wharf and chief landing, S12a resource sites: wood edge, clay pits, shore); field-driving classes (church, manor); source-oriented by depth from resources (charcoal pit, wood yard, potter, tannery); balanced (smithy); market-oriented (bakehouse, alehouse, inn, shop); ties by class id then member ordinal; one bounded relaxation pass (item 105 (f); at most base cap 2, on alloc.block) re-scores two-way classes, at village rungs moving an institution only between slots not yet raced. Then per block each remaining slot i draws u_i on village.slot keyed by lineage, key k_i = −ln(u_i) / max(1e-6, density_i^p x m_i), p = race.densityPower; block's remaining quota of dwellings goes to smallest keys (weighted draw without replacement = VG accept-with-density look at exact count; J-V7.8).

Village class mix (S10b generation fill; item 71 rows at village rungs, own): squalid -> v.hovel on squalid toft row; poor -> v.cottage 0.7, v.hovel 0.2, v.longhouse 0.1; modest -> v.cottage 0.5, v.farmstead 0.3, v.longhouse 0.2; comfortable -> v.farmstead 0.7, v.cottage 0.3; prosperous -> v.yeoman_house 0.5, v.farmstead 0.5; rich -> v.yeoman_house (manor only by its own row); v.longhouse weights x cultureForms' longhouse factor. Among equal slots larger classes take the sunnier (item 102 (d)). Every unbuilt slot becomes a close: joined to the built toft beside it on the same run with probability 0.5, else its own close plot held by the nearest built dwelling's household, yard part paddock/orchard/garden by the household's band; orchards false -> no orchard parts.

Moated manor: when the manor row's moated-site draw (0.25 with water within 150 m, on siteplan keyed by plot) succeeds, S11 lays two yard parts: a platform holding hall and chamber block, and a moat ring 5-8 m wide around it crossed by one drive part at the gate, drawn in the water tone, not a carved water body (no L0 batch after S10; J-V7.13); the platform part is the manor's levelled unit on a slope. Wells, closes and drives are the only non-building contents a toft adds. Capacity: after VS6's first three rungs, when laid slots still cannot hold D_v and institutions, S10a and S10b run F-V-SLOT's last two (doubled share to templates' households.max, then the report, never a drop); surplus slots are closes.

Levelling (item 110 (a); J-V7.84-89): plot/block/ward units are the wrong size in a village (toft-and-croft plot up to 380 m deep; block = whole face; ward = the one district); levelled unit = house platform; S11 levels after the site plan and before deriveBase. (1) For each built plot: union of building footprints grown by terrace.apronM (4 m) clipped to the toft yard part (manor: its platform part where the moat draw laid one; institution: the yard part holding its buildings, churchyard excluded); least-squares plane on at most fitSamples (12) samples of the base's refined 2.5 m raster (outline vertices simplified to at most 8, 4 interior points on diagonals at 1/3 and 2/3); when terrace.enabled and gradient > terrace.slopeMin (V11 TOWN value by reference) the platform is levelled at datum = mean of samples (cut fills fill; J-V7.84), published as levelled ground via the base's S10/S11 levelling output (C4-110-7), read by deriveBase (§2.2 datum), §8.4 shadows and V04 footing reach; below threshold follows ground (base plinth and skirt). (2) Walls: along each levelled platform's edge step abs(datum − natural ground) sampled every edgeSampleM (2.5 m); each maximal interval with step > stepMinCm (V11's by reference) is one generated RetainingWall (keyed §2.5), step profile the sampled steps, high side the platform on a fill edge and natural ground on a cut edge; material = base RetainingWall material row at the geology (dry stone by the village row, V11); step > stepMaxCm splits the platform along the contour into two levels each at its own datum (footprints split by the base's stepped-wing rule); a level shallower than minDepthM (V11 minTerraceDepthM) not levelled (whole platform keeps skirt and stepped wings); adjoining platforms share one wall (owner rule §2.5), step = datum difference.

(3) Never levelled by generation at village rungs: croft, close (incl. reached close), reached ground, green, churchyard part, pound, charcoal pit, a raised way's under-deck strip, every hinterland face (author may level by T2 terrace stroke or T3 retaining). (4) Longhouse exempt (J-V7.86): never levelled, skirt and stepped wings carry the fall, byre end downslope. (5) No district-edge source for fabric village-ways at any rung (village district and old core after hand-off up; J-V7.85), keyed by fabric not rung or district kind; hook FabricStrategy.levelledUnits (BCR-V7-34): bent cut returns item 110 (a)'s blocks, plots, wards and declares terraced edges; village-ways returns house platforms and declares none. (6) Stairs and ramps (J-V7.88): where a platform wall separates main door from frontage S11 lays the path as a stair yard part when step > terrace.stairFromCm (60 cm), else a ramp; class drive part as a ramp of grade <= rules.grade.track (20 %) laid along the wall inside the toft yard (dog-leg) when a straight ramp would be steeper; failing both F-V-TERRACE; stair and ramp are data-row yard-part kinds. (7) Village way-class crossing rule (item 110 (a); threshold terrace.stairFromCm): where a way crosses a retaining wall (drawn, terrace stroke edge, or a shrunk town's standing wall) through, secondary and track cross as ramps only within rules.grade; lane and path as a stair where step > stairFromCm else a ramp; never a gap; house platforms' own walls crossed only by plots' accesses. (8) Levelling S11's per plot, draw-free; walls and yard parts plot-level writes never L1 (writer order, T-V7-3 hold); re-deriving one plot re-levels it and its shared wall only. (9) Decline (J-V7.89): generated wall re-derives only while its dwelling stands short of cleared; then kept and decays by stretch. With heart.slopeMax 0.1 and VS2 slope term from 0.15 platforms mainly in hilly/mountainous villages; field terraces and strip lynchets not generated (J-V7.87; author's T2 stroke).

Land budget: FarmTable village rows (§4.9; own, calibratable) restate §2.2's haPerHead: arable 1.2 ha per head incl. fallow (arableHaPerCapita), meadow 0.15, pasture and commons 0.6, fuel 1.0 m3 per head-year against coppice at 4 m3/ha-year (0.25 ha), timber 0.15 m3 against 2 m3/ha (0.075 ha) (base fuel and timber law at its own defaults; village and town read one table); extent 'demand' at village rungs (frame remainder wildwood and waste); request arableFactor multiplies arable demand (absent 1). VG preset claims VG's field area vg.fieldM2PerDwelling (490 m2) per dwelling x arableFactor (farmland 4, uncultivated 0; D5.12), land decorative not fed (J-V7.12); under VG vg.fieldOneHouse (field holding more than one house discarded) and vg.orchardOnHouse (field overlapped by exactly one house becomes an orchard unless orchards false).

Suitability and outward claim (soft rule rows, own): arable = fertile x (1 − slope/0.15)+ x dry x sqrt(D) x (1 − dist/3 km)+; meadow = [below flood line] x damp x near water; pasture and commons = open ground rising with slope, distance, poor soil; wood = slope >= 0.2 or low D or frame wood propensity, rising with distance, x2 under forest 'many'; orchard = ring 1 beside tofts x D (0 when orchards false); D = item 102 daylight share (woods take shaded north slopes, fields and orchards sunny; woodShade 0.3); uses claim faces outward from the perimeter in 100 m bands (VG outward claim re-derived for a perimeter, as §4.9), within a band by suitability then face address: arable to demand, meadow to demand on flood ground, pasture and commons, coppice, managed wood; rest wildwood (waste above tree line or on rock); faces beneath a raised way claimed as any other, supports as holes. forest: many doubles wood claim, some leaves it, grove reverses (woods only in ring nearest perimeter). Under VG woods follow vg.forestMode fill/patches/grove, trees cleared within clearHouseM (7 m) of a house and clearWayM (5 m) of a way; crowns on render.instances, rerollable alone by rerollLayer('forest') (T10).

Field systems (S0 draw; factor rows as §2.2a): open_field (default at VILLAGE): arable divided into G great fields (3, or 2 when era row or poor land says) as angular sectors around the heart bounded by roads out, rebalanced by moving whole faces between neighbouring sectors until each holds arable/G ±25 %; each a VillageField great_field with rotation slot (winter grain, spring crop, fallow; §4.9 three-field rows per great field); hinterland unit cuts furlongs of 2-8 ha bounded by contours and field tracks; furrowAxisCdeg downslope where slope > 2 %, else perpendicular to access way; headlands = L3 path faces 5 m wide along furlong ends; strips = render-time segmentation along furrow axis at stripWidthM (10 m; 5-20 m by era); no hedges (balks drawn). enclosed: §4.9 enclosed fields (hedged, 1-5 ha), outlying farmsteads by their fields. infield_outfield: arable within 400 m of perimeter (about a third) = infield (rotation continuous), rest outfield cropped in slot 0 of a five-year cycle and grazed otherwise; hill ground common grazing; two VillageFields. forest_strip (row or street form only): each toft on the spine continues as one strip of its own width perpendicular to the street from its croft's rear line (croft untouched, T-V7-17) to wood edge or territory back line (at most stripMaxM 1.5 km), cut by extending plot side lines as L3 field lines, each a VillageField strip_holding with holder = its toft's plot (clerk, GeoJSON village_fields holder, §3.12 desertion returns strip to common); no outlying farms. vg_sector and mfcg_belt: §4.9's recorded sector constructions (P17, P18) unchanged.

(4) Meadow faces along water form a meadow field; pasture and commons one or more common fields (a common per 200 ha, split along roads); coppice and managed wood form wood fields; the green is the inner common (Greenery commons-owned); the fair field is claimed as a common face before the outward claim and joins the nearest common field. (5) Outlying farmsteads: D_o = ceil(H_o / householdsPerFarmstead) (§4.9 FarmTable; mode by form, BCR-V7-7) housing H_o households: sited first at approaches' ends (VG farmstead at approach end, D5) facing along the track, then by §4.9's farmstead score on fertile land near a track; each an outside plot with its drive; where a field face overruns an approach (VG trail repair) the approach is cut at the field edge and its farmstead moved there facing the edge (D5). (6) Decorations (§4.9 village rows): fishponds within 300 m of a manor (0.5), warren of pillow mounds on a common (0.2 with manor), boundary stones where roads cross the frame, wayside cross per through road, gallows hill on a through road at the frame (VILLAGE 0.1, seigneurial only).

Wharf, landings and piers (VS4 seeding step 5; VG D5.11; laid in VS4's L1 batch; pier count reads S2's dwelling count D; J-V7.51): wharf only on navigable water (coast, island's sea, estuary, river) with a dockable run (longest shore run with all points >= populated containing the densest shore point); shallow width s = 14 m + sqrt(0.7 x (w − 14 m) x 1 m) on a river of width w (14 m below that width), 28 m x (1 + F4) on coast or estuary, 20 m x (1.5 + B3) on a lake; pier length L = s x 1.5^S; river takes no wharf when L > w/2; wharf = quay way along the dockable run smoothed by two corner-cutting passes, resampled near L(1 + F4), stretch within one step of a bridge end removed, road inland from its densest vertex; piers 1 + floor(sqrt(5 D / (4 L / 0.7 m)) + u) pier ways of length L along the outward normal at wharf vertices where the point 1.5 L out is water, no pier crosses another, no bridge end within s; wharf trimmed from a random end (never its densest vertex) to that count. Without a wharf each Landing with no bridge nearby takes a single pier s(1 − F4/2) long when it fits the river's maximum. v.landing placed at wharf or busiest landing by S10b's row. Draws on village.slot keyed by wharf lineage; chief pier's head laid with it.

VS8 ends (J-V7.20): anchors in order: each open space (green), church, manor, mill, each part-0 bridge or ford (crossing; raised way never), each through-road entry within perimeter (entry), wharf or chief landing (wharf), each nucleus after the first (nucleus), each unmatched dossier naming claim (claim), each declared end; plots inside a declared end's lasso join it; every other plot joins the nearest anchor by walking distance along the ways; a derived anchor with fewer than ends.minPlots (6) plots merges into its nearest neighbour's end; derived ends capped at 1 + floor(households / 25), at most 6 ('1 at 40 people, 2 at 200, 6 from 625'), smallest merged first; declared ends exempt from merge and cap (item 101 R13; J-V7.71); end's plots derived, outline = union of plots' faces. An end is never assigned to a trade (item 107 (e)): anchors are places; a trade or chain names an end only by the dossier (quarter record claim, or a QUARTER ladder record claiming the end holding most of its members and owning them), by declareEnd, or by item 72's quarter-identity threshold crossed in that end (rarely reached).

VS8 pins and decorations (pin.centrepiece, pin.decor keyed by host): open space centrepiece; wells by coverage (one per 8 households within 120 m of their dwellings; an unbroken aqueduct delivery point counts) on the green, at junctions or in yards, pump from era row's pump date; moot place under chartered or council government (large tree or cross on the green beside the reeve's house); cross at a crossroads inside perimeter (0.4); stocks near church or on green (VILLAGE 0.5; BCR-V7-6); maypole on a green (0.2); shrine at perimeter on a road (0.3; dossier Roadside Shrine forces it); troughs at wells on through roads (0.3); on an open space carrying the market: stalls (stall pins) one per stalls.perHouseholds (40) households, at least stalls.min (3), along the rim facing the ways (a street market along the through road's frontage nearest the heart where an epoch gave a market to a village with no open space, §3.12 (d)).

Pin-record rule (SR4-01; J-V7.127): after the rows above, a @pin:<kind> record (V11 §3.11) binds to a standing pin of its kind within presence.siteReachM of the frame centre that no other record binds, nearest the heart first; where none remains it is given one pin of that kind in VS8's batch, drawn on pin.decor keyed by the record's binding key (provenance names the record), and binds to it; shrine placed as the shrine row places it; market_cross stands at the centre of the reservation carrying the market (open space or flanking square), replacing the centrepiece §3.6 (5) drew there or standing where none was drawn; at an epoch or absorb it replaces only an engine-placed centrepiece no one holds (tombstoned in that batch, a listed fate), otherwise stands beside it (TW-06); with no such reservation (epoch street market) on the through road's frontage nearest the heart beside the stalls; a well record (water_source) binds to coverage wells as multiple_water_sources binds its members, giving a well only where none stands; churchyard cross of a wayside shrine merged into a parish church laid in the churchyard part nearest the church door whatever other crosses stand, shrine record binds it, save after a promotion receipt when the cross is laid for the promoted record with no binding row and the record's one key binds the church (V08 §3.5.1 (d); J-V8.114), such a cross a forced pin tombstoned by remove with it (J-V7.130); no edge shrine placed for that record; same rule runs in village.records at a village epoch or absorb and for a pin-record lesser whose REPLACEMENT greater arrives.

These rows are the village's whole furniture (SR3-02; J-V7.118): at territory-frame rungs S11's furniture step (§4.7 Furniture pins: centrepieces, gate plazas' pins, blocks' decoration rows, singletons, campfires, market stalls by rank) places no pin (BCR-V7-38); open space carries only VS8's centrepiece and stalls; fair field carries none (fair booths never drawn); no village stage or furniture step places a statue, fountain, bandstand or monument at a village rung; a handed-down town's standing pins stay as standing fabric (TV-03); S11's light rows (item 68) run unchanged (V07 §5.1 night); at a village epoch the rows run through village.pins.

Names (S13a, §10.4; naming; rows = V11 §3.20.1's naming.settlement village features, naming.villageEnd, naming.field; SS-18): village name from own grammar rows with own descriptive tags (water type, form, relief, rung, palisade, part-0 bridge or ford, wood) — the idea of tags feeding names is VG's, its grammar and word lists never used (§17.1); each end by its kind's pattern rows (church end, mill end, town's end at an entry, green side, wick for a nucleus); lane names at VILLAGE for lanes an anchor gives (mill lane, church lane, back lane); each great field by bearing from the heart; each common and wood by use and place; dossier names protected (DR14).

Deck plots at village rungs (item 110 (d); J-V7.91): generation makes one kind only, a widened pier head with the landing's net store; every other is the author's. (1) Eligible decks: VS4's pier ways and part-0 bridge decks; the wharf (a shore quay way on land) carries none; a raised deck carries none (V02 J-V2.71; V1 I110R-5). (2) Widths (BCR-V7-25 as amended; own, calibratable): pier 2.5 m, quay 5 m, bridge deck its carried way's width + 2 x parapetM (1 m in all), ford its carried way's width; a deck face is buildable where (deck width − way width) / sides reaches V11 §3.24.4 minPlotDepthM for its kind, so no default pier or bridge qualifies; only a pier head (as deep as deck.headM) or an author-widened deck (setAttr of its width) carries a plot. (3) Pier head: when S2's roster holds a v.landing, the chief pier (nearest the wharf's densest vertex, else the single landing pier) ends in a head of deck.headM (8 m along x 6 m wide) with probability deck.headChance PLaw (200, 0) -> (700, 0.3) -> (1 500, 0.5), drawn on village.slot keyed <pier>/head, laid in VS4's L1 batch within the pier's length; S10 lays its one deck plot by the base deck-plot rule owned by the landing's institution; S10b stands the net store (else boat shed) as a structure of the landing's compound, composed by V02 @deck rows via DeckContext within the deck budget (X16). (4) Uses: no dwelling; deckOk with the village reading (J-V7.41): store, net shed, boat shed; toll house or chapel only by author's or dossier record; deck plots outside S10a quotas and VS6 capacity (D_v, race, T-V7-2 unchanged). (5) Containment: VS5 unites deck faces of piers and bridges with a foot inside the perimeter; a deck face outside belongs to the hinterland pseudo-district. (6) Lifecycle: falls with its deck by least disruption (V06 flood), rebuilt deck re-offers it. (7) Under VG headChance 0.

Routing: the village package registers ProductDecl (range [1, 1 500)) in StrategyRegistry.products, consulted by the one port through LadderRouter (file f item 202; SS-19): every SF thorp (8-60), hamlet (61-400), village (401-900) and town 901-1 499 (research/sf/mapping.md T1: 70 of 70 small dossiers, 5 of 38 towns in the surveyed 155) is created on the village rows; port stops refusing it (§1.1's refusal names the village product only while none is registered); rung follows population (DR23); the dossier's tier word titles the map (§9.5): a 1 105-person SF town drawn on VILLAGE rung, titled a town.

What a small dossier holds (research/sf/dossier-outputs.md §3.4, §6): one population integer; a tier word; 7-42 institution records incl. one housing record with a count range (4-16, 17-80 or 80-180 dwellings); a government name (elder or household council, feudal stewardship, elected reeve); terrain word, access word, deposit keys; a wall record in 6-8 of 20 dossiers per tier (hasWalls and hasGates together); 0-2 quarters with fixed location phrases (Religious Quarter, Alehouse & Common, Fishing Landing, Woodcutters' Ground, Roadside Shrine; small towns' Market Quarter); 0-4 landmark strings; culture, wealth, power records; no port institution below the town tier; no coordinates. Every gap derived by our rules (items 20 (h), 22).

Religious Quarter's east phrase ('Eastern district (traditional)'): parish church siting gains the base's soft east row at its low weight (§7.7 item 16 quarter row, tables/dossier/quarters), church end tends east — 'a placeholder the owner may drop (J80 Q5)', with which T-V7-13's east clause lapses. DR7 households (J-V7.55): H0 = round(P / meanSize); with the housing range [min, max]: (1) too few (H0 < min): H = min(min, max(1, floor(P / household.minSize))), mean size P/H never below minSize (1.5), D = min, one household a dwelling; when H < min the min − H surplus dwellings built vacant and reported W_VACANT_TO_RANGE (e.g. 10-person thorp, range 4-16: H0 = 2, H = 4, D = 4, sizes 3, 3, 2, 2); (2) otherwise H = H0 and D_raw = sum_b round(H_b / (1 + share2_b)); if D_raw > max the doubling re-solved band by band from the poorest up, at most two households a dwelling, until D = max; if full doubling leaves ceil(H/2) > max, household size rises (H = 2 max), reported; if D_raw < min doubling undone band by band from the richest doubling band down until D = min; (3) members sum to P exactly: each household floor(P/H), remainder one each in address order. D = D_v + D_o (outlying farmsteads count as dwellings); residential count in the record's range (DR7's bar); every household housed once.

(3) a class with its own row plays itself at any rung once named (pawnshop, smugglers_store); (4) only a kind that fell to V11's generic-<family> takes the tag fallback, the port's one unmapped_kind note naming the class given (V08 §4.6; SR4-07, SR4-08), no second report: religious -> v.parish_church from 400 people else v.chapel; market -> open space's market; lodging -> v.inn on a through road else v.alehouse; food with keyword brewer, brewery (food-works), tavern or alehouse (lodging) -> v.alehouse; metalwork -> v.smithy; food keyword with key mill -> v.watermill else v.windmill; law_enforcement or defense -> v.watchtower; civic or legal -> v.reeve_house; healing -> V11 healer class on a toft slot (dwelling-row template read as dwelling plot;
