(6) Surface marker (item 109 (b); J-V7.81): at village rungs S12a sites the ruin decoration (§4.9 decoration table village row, hinterland.decor) for a dossier ancient_ruins deposit or ruined-landmark record on the most prominent hinterland face within ruinMarker.maxM (800 m) of the heart that no arable claim takes, else nearest open ground; a ruined-landmark record's building stands there as a roofless shell (V02 ruined-landmark composition) or V02's stepped-monument composition when the ancient-culture row builds in tiers (V04 monument rule, C4-110-8; V02 §3.15.6; J-V7.94); marker = RuinRecord.marker, the ruin's centre and its ruin-entrance candidate; without a dossier source no marker until an opening or excavation makes one; unexcavated style and toggle V09's; explanations V10's. (7) Over time: every building village siting adds over a void draws once (accessible share rises with growth); excavation, sealing, ruin decay are V06's scheduling over V04's rules; both hand-offs carry voids, access points, dwellings unchanged. (8) Tail runs after first paint (V04 §3.1), draws on sewer; with ruin chance 0 and the base relief, boost and fissure rows the village is byte-identical to the build without these kinds (T-V7-38); cost = V04 §6's village columns (whole tail <= 10 ms p95 at each village rung, after first paint, outside §6's model law).

Editing: everything a village has is editable with item 101's twelve tools (§7.1 authoring toolkit); village adds no thirteenth tool — two parameters and one sugar event (BCR-V7-19); every declaration held (§7.2) until its author changes it, bent to the nearest lawful form by its dry run otherwise (item 101 R2).

Twelve tools on a village: T1 intend — site card with form, water, palisade, field system, organic roads, orchards, forest, field factor; size = population; density and wealth sliders; events recipe intent at creation, afterwards Adjust / Re-derive on VillageRequest; a form edit making a held forest_strip unlawful bent to open_field with a note; derived by S0. T2 ground — reshape ground, draw brook or pond, move course-first river knots (WaterBody.controls), draw a terrace (item 110 (a): faces under the stroke levelled and walled along its edge, field terrace or lynchet included; J-V7.87); events setField(terrain), warp, drawWater, moveCourseKnot, terrace stroke (V09 terrace sugar) whose edge is a drawn RetainingWall where step > terrace.stepMinCm, held; derived by S1 operators, S10-S11 levelling inside perimeter, hinterland unit outside. T3 wall — palisade, bank and ditch, stone circuit; add gate; river, cliff or marsh closes it; retaining wall held never an enclosure; drawWall kind palisade/earthwork/inner/retaining (high side by drawing direction or ground; plots crossed re-levelled; ways crossed become stair or ramp by §3.8a (7)); points form derives the village trace (VS3 smoothing and pull, closing when ends meet); stretch end snaps to a barrier within reach, barrier arcs shown (item 106 (g), V09 snapping); placeGate; derived by VS3 steps 5-6, S7. T4 road — draw road, lane, track between points or walk from a point; raised way or aqueduct (any rung); drawWay with class; walk {headingCdeg, class road/track, maxLengthM?} (dry run runs one tracker, branches off, stores laid spine resolved); raised true or aqueduct class by points only (walk with raised bent to points form with a note); count badge; derived by S4 router (points) or VS4 tracker (walk); raised by base raised-part commit.

Tools cont.: T5 quarter — at a village rung declare an end by lassoing its houses (item 101 R4), kind and name; anchor defaults to most significant entity inside (church, manor, mill, open space, else lasso centroid) or picked; sugar quarter expands to declareEnd with boundary (BCR-V7-19); count badge; derived by VS8. T6 place — heart, church, mill, manor, well, centrepiece; assign a use; on a deck face (pier head or widened bridge) a store, net shed, boat shed, toll house or chapel; placeAt (heart = placeAt of VillagePlan.heart, heartSource edit), assign, build; on a deck face S10b's request path with deckOk in the village reading (dwelling there bent to nearest toft with a note); derived by VS1 (heart), S10b (mill bent to nearest mill seat). T7 roster — list what the village must hold; with a dossier the author may only place (§7.1); S10b claims-first. T8 fill — brush more/fewer houses, draw a green, brush class mix; setField(density), drawGreen kind green (green Reservation and Greenery); S10a quotas and slot race in touched blocks. T9 shape — split/join tofts, build on a close, move a house, set croft depth, change a furlong's strips; split, join, build, moveFootprint, setAttr (yard parts, furrowAxisCdeg, rotation.slot), drawFootprint. T10 hold — lock, pin, revert, regenerate; New random on a block re-races slots, on the plan redraws auto draws; rerollLayer('village.track') re-grows roads; rerollLayer('forest') re-draws crowns. T11 name — setAttr(name) on VillageEnd, VillageField, reservation, way; moveLabel, hideLabel, group. T12 dress — painterly or ink; fields, relief, spotlight, shade map, underground (unexcavated voids, V09 toggle); setStyle, setLayer, paintGround. delete (V09 §4.3) — remove a raised way: declared = V09 delete of its declaration; carried generated = C6-39 suppression (reason key in log), dry run 'the town will not rebuild this aqueduct; undo brings it back'.

Other village edits: land conversion by hand = convert with retypeLand (file f item 209 absorbing BCR-V7-22; ST-25) under T2's land-use chip; retiring, effacing, reopening a way by hand = convert with retireWay/effaceWay/reopenWay (BCR-V7-32 (b)) under T4's way chip, dry run keeps every live plot's access (a stretch that is some plot's only access stays in use with a note); underground edited with V04's tools and events (drawTunnel, drawChamber with system ruin or cavern, addUndergroundAccess, closure states; V04 §4), lifecycle and undo V04's; a church's crypt is its building's basement (V02, V03 events). Count badge (item 101 R14): dry runs of declareEnd, drawGreen, density brush, raised way add/removal, retaining wall, terrace stroke show plots, households, buildings touched. Supply links (item 105 (j)) pinned, moved or cut by base link events through V09's link view, stored map-side, never written to the dossier (a cut bakehouse-mill link makes flour an import). Author split: T6 assign of the shop to a second plot with branchOf naming the works' use (BCR-V7-24), held, merged back by inverse. Item 110 declarations (drawn wall, terrace stroke, declared raised way, placed deck plot) held through Regenerate (keep); generated wall edited by setAttr of material or by drawing over (drawn wall wins); deck widened by setAttr of width (face buildable).

New event forms (BCR-V7-19): EditEvent gains {t: 'declareEnd'; anchor?: Id or PointCm (absent: most significant entity inside boundary); boundary?: PolygonCm; kind: VillageEnd kind; name?} (sugar quarter expands to it at a village rung; creates a declared VillageEnd keyed by the event's address, held); drawWay gains optional walk {headingCdeg; class road/track; maxLengthM?} (one tracker from points[0] by VS4 step rules, branches off; laid spine resolved into points at dry run); walk and raised are exclusive (bent to the points form with a note, item 101 R2); retypeLand is V06's EvolveOp member, one op for both volumes (file f item 209; ST-25): {op: 'retypeLand'; landUse; to: LandUse kind; crop?; rotation? {scheme, slot}}. setAttr reaches VillagePlan.form, .roads, .nuclei, .character.*, VillageRequest.*, Reservation.kind between green and plaza, Enceinte.kind among village kinds, VillageField.name and .kind, VillageEnd.name, each with base dry run, fate report, inverse (§7.1, §7.4).

Locality per village edit (§7.3): heart moved / form or road topology changed / nuclei edited -> from VS1; settlement VS1-VS8 and S7-S11 on the district; hinterland only on faces the perimeter move touches; locked/pinned held, declared re-placed; coarse 'the village is re-laid around the new heart; N houses move'. Character -> VS4, network and after in the district. Density brush -> S10a, touched blocks (quotas re-allocated among themselves, sum kept; re-raced), 'N houses in the brushed blocks'. drawGreen -> VS4 open-space step for the green only then VS6-S11, blocks overlapped or fronting. drawWall (village kinds) -> VS3's form then S7, the wall's band cleared and re-cut, gates where ways cross. drawWay (points or walk) -> VS6 on faces it splits. declareEnd -> VS8, ends only (count badge). Class placed/assigned -> S10b request path, target plot and relocated occupants (§4.7). Market hall claim or fair field moved (T6 placeAt of its member) -> VS4 claim step along the rim or VS5 fair step at the point; open space remainder and hall plot, or fair field face and commons around (S12a). Field system changed -> S12a, hinterland faces, outlying farmsteads re-sited, nothing inside perimeter. retypeLand, rotation.slot, furrowAxisCdeg -> hinterland unit on that face. retireWay/effaceWay/reopenWay -> the network's readers of that way, way alone (no live plot's access from a hollow way; a reopened way's runs raced again only by regrowth). New random on a block -> that block. rerollLayer('village.track') -> VS4 as character edit. T3 retaining -> S10-S11 in plots crossed (re-levelled, re-cut; stair or ramp for a crossed way). T2 terrace stroke -> S10-S11 inside, hinterland unit outside. T4 raised way added -> §3.5a (10) (blocks re-raced with quotas kept, shortfall to neighbours; faces re-cut; feet joined; well coverage). Raised way removed -> strip blocks re-raced, faces re-cut, V04 vaults removed same commit. Deck plot placed -> S10b request path on the deck face. Deck widened -> S10 on the deck face ('the pier head can now hold a shed'). Coarse edits declared coarse by dry run (§7.3); a density stroke never moves a quota outside its blocks.

Edit lifecycle (§7.4 columns): declareEnd — event (sugar quarter); VS8, labels, exports; log; held (lasso plots re-joined every re-derivation; never merged or capped); inverse removes the end; event schema version, an event without boundary reads a point declaration. drawWay with walk — event with resolved spine stored; VS6 on split faces; log; never re-walked (spine is the recorded input); inverse removes the way, faces re-joined; as drawWay. retypeLand (one lifecycle row with V06's, file f item 209) — convert or epoch op; S12b, hinterland unit, render; log or epoch record; kept; conversion's undo record; new op kind versioned. retireWay/effaceWay/reopenWay — event or epoch op; network readers (hollow way read by none), hollow_way role, GeoJSON hollow_ways; kept; conversion undo; new op kinds. setAttr on VillagePlan, VillageRequest, VillageField, VillageEnd — event; §2.6 rows; log; recorded value read on regenerate; inverse. Village density stroke — setField(density); S10a, race; log (strokes); composited onto recomputed raster (§7.2); stroke inverse. drawGreen (kind green) — held (declared); inverse. drawWall retaining; T2 terrace stroke — event; S10-S11 levelling, hinterland unit, render, exports, clerk; log; held; inverse; older document nothing. drawWay raised or aqueduct — event; §3.5a stages, V04 arch-vault source; log; held, feet re-joined at every derivation; inverse. Raised way removal (V09 delete; C6-39 suppression) — event; declaration layer (raised), V6 §3.19 ledger from first CITY epoch; log (reason key for a generated way); held through Regenerate (keep), every village epoch and both hand-offs; inverse restores way and vaults with their ids. Deck plot placed; deck widened — event; S10b, V02 DeckContext, render; log; held while its deck stands, falls with its deck and re-offered when rebuilt; inverse.

Clerk's view (V10 over §11.2's tool API): reads the same records a person sees (VillagePlan, ends, fields, palisade, dossier facts); proposes with the twelve tools as dry runs shown as ghosts (J-A101.74). Describe-to-map returns a skeleton, e.g. 'a green village by a ford...' -> intend (VILLAGE, 600 people, form green, water stream), place (v.parish_church, high ground within 200 m of heart), place (v.watermill), intend (field system open_field), never a picture. 'Why is this here' answers from rows that pulled it: heart from VS1 score terms; house from slot density, rim multiplier, block quota; class from §2.4 profile, relation and coverage rows, signature pairs fired (item 103 (e)); wood from §3.9 suitability incl. shade (item 102 (f)); custom institution from resolved profile sources (item 104 (a)); trade from links and goods (item 105 (j)) or coverage and spacing; market hall from its claim; fair field from its record; pin from forcing record or VS8 row and epoch (provenance; SR4-01, TV-03); unwalled side from the barrier arc (item 106 (g)); ladder record from its members; underground from V04 records (V10 rows): unexcavated void, access cause, dwelling from its access; crypt or its absence; burial face; strip holding's holder; hollow way's disuse epoch; item 110 (V10 rows): generated wall from platform step ('the ground falls 22 % here'), carried raised way from reason and year, removal, absence ('villages never build them; you may draw one'), pier head, scarp.

Painterly family: the village opens in 'painterly' (base reserves the slot, §8.2; V07 builds it at all four bands); every other family draws a village from the same display list (§8.1), ink one click away (J-V7.25); style sheet is data (roles, programs, layer order, palette on §8.2 targets, item 69; own colours never VG's, §17.1). Programs (PaintProgram in §8.2's registry): Ground: ground ramp by relief class and moisture over paper tone; base hillshade (multiply shade side, add lit side, at 0.5 and 0.25 strength); relief tier on (contours, hachures or grass marks by the sheet's relief option; grass default: short slope-aligned ticks alternately longer/shorter, light or dark by facing). Water: water-band law of §8.3's census (W x (i/N)^1.5, N = 3), stony edge as a pair of jittered strokes along every shore, one tide line on flowing water and two on still water and sea (ref:VG water look, D5, geometry only). Ways: through wide, street narrow, lanes narrower, tracks dotted (dash 1 % of width, gap two widths), driveways as flared patches, junction corner fills where roads meet at > 26 deg; fords a pale band with stepping marks; hollow ways a sunken double hairline with inner shade; way.edgeFade: a road leaving the frame turns over its last fadeM (60 m) into a dotted trail whose dot spacing widens x1.4 per dot; bridge.shadow = deck.shadow for a part-0 bridge (offset band along §8.4's sun, offset = deck height x sun cotangent); pier head = widened plank deck; way.stair: step ticks one per stairTickM (0.3 m) of run, tick side toward low end (V1 I110-2); way.ramp: tapered wedge tint darkest at low end.

Painterly cont.: Fields: each furlong in its crop tone with bounded jitter; strips as furrow strokes along furrowAxisCdeg at strip width, dashed from a small set of patterns, headlands plain; enclosed fields hedged by hedgerow instances (§8.10); orchards rows of crowns (jittered grid, §4.9); meadow fine stipple, commons coarse; great-field boundaries faint dashed at township band. Woods: crown.bands (rim band of full crowns, one or two muted bands offset inward at mutedMix 0.35 toward fill tone, solid interior billowed thicket fill); crown.groupShade (each crown shaded away from light; touching crowns shaded as one mass; per-crown radial gradient a sheet option, off in ink); crowns from §8.10 instances on render.instances (never stored), rerollLayer('forest') redraws them alone. Palisade: thick dark line with stake ticks every 1.5 m outside; earthwork bank of short hachures toward the ditch with the ditch a thin water-toned or dark line outside; inner stone circuit as ink's wall symbol at half width; gates a gap with two posts or a gatehouse footprint; light stretch at half weight (wattle thin line with cross-hatches, low bank sparse hachures, parapet stone symbol at a third width); barrier anchor post dot (palisade, earthwork) or small tower (stone); closing arcs drawn only as their barrier; the wall layer's 'show circuit' option (V09) traces them faint dashed.

Painterly buildings (J-V7.73): roof shapes are V02's roof rows (gable default for cottages and longhouses, hip for manor and church nave by templates); roof.faces: each roof drawn as its planes, lit faces in the roof tone, unlit mixed toward shadow by unlitMix (0.45), a pair of hatch strokes alternating across the ridge at hatchM (0.8 m) parallel to the fall, plus entrance mark (V02 entrance); roof.palette: weighted list (thatch, tile, slate, shingle; about one in three slate where geology gives slate), per-building tone variance ± roofJitter (6 %) keyed by lineage; roof.oblique: oblique extrusion by height x obliqueShare, sheet option off by default (base no-oblique-default rule); roof.ruin: ruined or decayed building as wall ring with gaps and no roof, cleared as footprint trace = house platform (low rectangle with hachured sides; levelled platform's kept walls drawn by retaining.wall in decay as the scarp); selective outlining (outline colour mix toward ink by outline pressure, §8.2) and cast shadows by the light model (§8.4; cursor sun on by default). Item 110 (J-V7.93; own cells): retaining.wall line weight follows step profile (hairline at stepMinCm, full weight at 300 cm and above), stone ticks toward low side every tickM (0.8 m), low-side cast shadow at wall height; decayed stretch a broken line with slumped stipple (scarp); raised.deck band drawn above everything it crosses in the way's tone with parapet hairlines, deck.shadow generalised to every deck (offset band on whatever lies beneath, offset = deck height above that surface x sun cotangent, per span), arch openings only under roof.oblique; raised.support small filled rectangles at district band and finer, only shadows at city band; raised.ruin: ruined span a gap with rubble stipple, cleared span plain gap; aqueduct.channel thin water-tone line along deck centre while unbroken, dry (deck tone) once broken; stepped tiers (V02 tier, shrine, stair roles, stairFlight): each tier by roof.faces at its height with its own cast shadow; deck-plot buildings unchanged, shadows on water.

Spotlight: radial vignette; spotlight.focus heart (default VillagePlan.heart), centre (view centre) or edge (pushed from heart toward the frame edge opposite the light along the shadow angle); spotlight.size radius as a share of the distance to the farthest visible corner (1 default); lightened centre fading out by half the radius, then a shade deepening from half the radius to the edge, intensities separate cells (ref:VG spotlight, D5.14: spotlight.core 0.2, spotlight.rim 0.8); a view program never entering the model; off in exports unless the sheet says so. Night: base night view (§8.4 (e), item 68): lit windows by occupancy, alehouse and inn lamps, no street lighting (era row public-lighting density at village rungs 0). Shade map (item 102 (f)): thematic view of the daylight share over settlement and fields from daylight.terrain with the palisade's shade (terrain and walls, item 102 (b)); a setLayer toggle, never on by default. Program cells (fadeM, dot factor, unlitMix, hatchM, roof weights, roofJitter, obliqueShare, mutedMix, spotlight's; stairTickM, tickM, wall-weight ramp) are the painterly sheet's own cells, own constants described as geometry never the reference's values (§17.1), each in B-ZOOM's role list (T-V7-25). Underground marks under a village are V04's programs and V09's toggle.

New roles (rows in every family's sheet with defaults so ink, lit and hatched draw them): village.green, village.close, village.croft, palisade, earthwork, palisade.light, wall.anchor, hollow_way, house_platform, strip_field, headland, great_field_edge, meadow, common, ford, village.pond_part (uncarved pond part in water tone), roof.ruin, landmark yard parts village.net_rack (two posts with a hatched span), village.drying_rack (short ladder of bars), village.timber_stack (rectangle of log-end rings) (named beach drawn by the base shore program as its beach run, no new role), item 110's retaining_wall, way.stair, way.ramp, raised.deck, raised.support, raised.ruin, aqueduct.channel ('or the base's names once the coherence pass fixes them'), pin symbols stocks and maypole (§8.3's symbol catalogue gains the two glyphs and well, pump, cross, market cross, shrine, trough and stall glyphs at village scale so every pin VS8, village.pins or a pin record places is drawn; SR4-01, TV-03).

Bands at village scale (§8.5 LodBand): city = whole township, fields as tones and strip hatching, settlement as masses; district = village with first fields, every footprint, way, wall; neighbourhood = tofts, crofts, closes with fences and hedges, wells, yards, green centrepiece; building = stage 3 (V02); no stage-2 close-up (J-V7.24). First view frames the perimeter's bounding box x1.6 (at least 400 m a side; rules.firstView) at the district band; township one zoom-out away (J-V7.4; BCR-V7-9); first paint is the complete district band (§8.5), relief tier, shadows, spotlight following within the settle bound (§12.5).

Labels (S13a builds, S13b places; §9.1, §9.2; collision-checked, never over a gate, the church or a well): title plate = village name, tier word (dossier's when bound, else the rung's), water qualifier from resolved water type (own row: riverside, by the sea, on the island, at the ford; plate.qualifier on by default in painterly), population rounded to plate.populationRound (1; 10 under VG) (§9.5 furniture as BCR-V7-31 extends it), in the corner covering fewest ways, never over the heart. Ends at the district band curved along the end's main way or straight across a green; green, church, manor, mill, inn as landmark labels; fair field (own word row else record name) at the district band, drawn as the common it is inside the base's secondary-market outline; named beach along its run; raised way as a landmark at district band by own word row ('the arches' for viaduct or elevated road, 'the aqueduct') unless named; lanes at neighbourhood band for lanes §3.10 named; the stream along its course; great fields, commons, woods at city band in letter-spaced italics; house numbers on request (§9.5 address numbers, VG's 'marked' look). Scale bar, compass, grid in metres, feet or squares (VG's 'vague' units removed, docs/improvements/vg.md §4 (2)).

Exports (§11.1): SVG and PNG by band and family; GeoJSON in metres; VTT scenes (district band: palisade and buildings as walls, gates as doors; and one at city band); glTF/OBJ with heights; CityJSON; .plat document; skeleton file (village request, declarations, ends). GeoJSON layers (id, kind, name each): village_plan (heart and nuclei points, radius), ends (union of each end's plots; declared), village_fields (great fields, infield, outfield, commons, meadow, woods, strip holdings as multipolygons with slot, system, holder), closes (reached), approaches (lines), open_spaces (greens and squares with market rank; fair field kind 'fair'; hall claim exports as its plot), hollow_ways (lines with disuse epoch), house_platforms (polygons of cleared dwellings, levelled), landmark_parts (net_rack, drying_rack, timber_stack polygons with kind, plot, landmark name; named beach LineString with bankKind 'beach' and name); retaining walls, raised parts (supports, spans), deck plots by the base's item 110 mappings; caverns, ruins, access points, crypts by V04's and V02's mappings; palisade as its enceinte; every new entity kind has its export mapping in the entity registry (§2.8 paths; BCR-V7-3) covered by the registry's completeness test.

Performance (§12.1 reference machine): VG's own model 14 ms (no water) to 143 ms (pond, cold), whole regenerate with rendering 240-330 ms script (research/findings/profile-village.md §5). Model time law (p95, §12.3 pool configuration, single-worker fallback +15 %): T <= 20 ms + 0.8 ms x frame km2 + 110 µs x footprints (J-V7.42, J-V7.61); frame term = frame with margin (1.44 x territory), from §12.4's hydrology rate (about 0.16 µs per cell). Bars: THORP 21/24/27 ms at bottom/target/top (frame 0.5/1.7/3.3 km2; 3/20/40 footprints), bar 30 ms; HAMLET 27/35/50 ms (3.3/8.3/16.5 km2; 40/75/150), bar 50 ms; VILLAGE 50/71/129 ms (16.6/29/62 km2; 150/250/540), bar 100 ms up to about 1 100 people, above it the law (<= 130 ms at top), a declared miss against TOWN's 100 ms one-click bar in §12.3's form.

VILLAGE target split (p50, PLAUSIBLE until V-M0): S0 0.2, S1 10 (terrain 8 m from 32 m fBm grid; hydrology 32 m about 28 000 cells), S2 1, VS1 4.5 (heart lattice 1; nine daylight sweeps <= 3 over about 72 000 cells, <= 6 at top over about 155 000; lattice, destinations, border, ponds 0.3; leat 0.2), VS2 6 (about 150 000 cells), VS3 0.4, VS4 4.5 (about 1 500 tracker steps, neighbour roads, wharf, piers), VS5 3, S7 1, S7b 0.5, S12a 3, VS6 1.5, S9-S11 18 (about 70 µs per footprint), S12b and hinterland unit 8 (about 400 furlong faces), VS8 1, S12c and S13a 2 = about 65 ms vs law's 71 ms. g items inside: barrier closure <= 0.5 ms in VS3; supply links and relaxation <= 1.5 ms in S10b (about 25 institutions, <= 2 passes); item 110: S11 levelling <= 1 ms at VILLAGE top (about 300 platforms), VS4 support test <= 0.2 ms (uniform grid index; only when a raised way stands); underground tail after first paint outside the law (V04 §6: <= 10 ms p95). First map: complete district band <= model time + 60 ms (<= 160 ms at top). Edits p95: block re-race <= 5 ms; density stroke over 10 blocks <= 15 ms; drawGreen <= 20 ms; drawWay <= 15 ms; declareEnd <= 3 ms (lassoed with count badge <= 5 ms); field system switch <= 15 ms; coarse edit <= rung's model time; drawn wall with barrier snapping <= 20 ms; link pinned or cut <= 5 ms; raised way added <= 20 ms, removal <= 15 ms; retaining wall drawn <= 15 ms; terrace stroke over 10 blocks <= 20 ms; deck plot placed <= 5 ms; underground edits V04 §6's. Epoch at VILLAGE target <= 60 ms (no S5), incl. village.pins <= 2 ms (coverage pass, orphan check, <= 10 new pins) and village.records <= 5 ms per record placed (fair field <= 3 ms; item 4's church the base's §12.6 row plus one pin), <= 1 ms per record remove takes; same per-record bounds on an absorb. Memory <= 25 MB at VILLAGE top. Work limits (§5.1 (5)): tracker steps <= 40 x frame side / step (top-ups included); trackers <= 4 + 0.3 D + 3; slots <= 3 D + institutions' joins; daylight sweeps 9 x cells. Confirming: V-M0 spike and V-M1 exit on B-VILLAGE. Pre-decided fallback: rung p95 over bar -> height raster 12 m, daylight 30 m, density 6 m at that rung, re-measured; still failing -> bar re-declared at measured p95 for owner's veto (D-18 form).

B-VILLAGE bench: 200 seeds per village rung x four water settings (none, stream, river, coast) x seven forms at default weights (PR tier 20 seeds per rung; nightly full; §13.8 tiers) plus frozen small-dossier fixtures (70 thorps, hamlets, villages and 5 small towns of the 155 surveyed) and the 10-person thorp fixture; plus B-VG: 200 seeds per VG request-tag set under VG, each mapped onto VillageRequest by the request-mapping table (BCR-V7-23). Bars labelled C (rule followed), P (parity with a measured VG number), O (outcome VG does not reach), as §13 labels them; a class named in words is its v. row (J-V7.95).

T-V7-1 (C, V-M1) routing: populations 1, 8, 79, 80, 399, 400, 1 499 build THORP, THORP, THORP, HAMLET, HAMLET, VILLAGE, VILLAGE; 1 500 builds a TOWN; unregistered product: dossier below 1 500 refused naming the village product; registered: created. T-V7-2 (C, V-M1/V-M2) population exact: members sum to P on every seed; D_v + D_o = D, every household housed once; with a dossier residential count in the housing range on every fixture; 10-person thorp (4-16) builds 4 households in 4 dwellings; fixture below minSize builds surplus vacant and reports W_VACANT_TO_RANGE. T-V7-3 (C, V-M1) registration: every input key has exactly one producer in the set (declaration layer = producer of declarations.* and raised); no village stage writes a ground part from 1; VS2 and VS3 before VS4, VS5 before S7; none of S3-S6, S8; L0 only by S1 and VS1; L1 only by VS1 (border first), VS4, VS5, S7, S7b, VS6 in order, none after S9 (kernel writer check).

Conventions: 'the base' is docs/ARCHITECTURE.md with amendments c, d, e folded in and file g items 102-110 as the coherence pass applies them; a § points into the base, 'V08 §' into this volume; SettlementForge field names and values quoted freely (owner's own project; amendments d, gate 2); no SF code excerpted; nothing from SF's map programs or map designs used; BCR-V8-n (§10), J-V8.n (§9), T-V8-n (§7).

Plain words: SF gets a Map tab on every settlement page; first opened by someone with GM rights, the map is drawn from the dossier (every listed institution sited sensibly, population fills the right number of houses, walls, gates, harbour and quarters match; everything unsaid derived by the map's rules from the same seed); the map never writes back into the dossier. On change (DM event, decree, week, season, year) the map compares the new dossier with facts it carries, works out what changed, reads each change's week from the dossier's receipts, changes the town as little as it can; history panel says what moved and why in SF's words ('bankrupt', 'destroyed by disaster'); after the DM advances time campaign maps catch up one by one in the background; a map opened before its turn catches up at once.

Plain words: custom institutions and chains from SF's homebrew library arrive like built-in ones; the map reads scene type, category and tags and (when handed over) the fuller library entry; an active supply chain laid out as one working line (raw material at its field or quarry, workshops stepping inward, seller near the market); renaming a custom item changes nothing; revising moves it only as far as needed. 'Blacksmiths (3-10)' drawn as several smithies, a guild as its hall with workshops, a 'district' as a quarter, never twice when SF lists the smaller form; SF supply chains tie mills, bakeries, markets together, a weakened chain pulls less; a coastal town whose record names a war or hostile sea partner walls its quays; a storm leaves damage where it struck; ancient ruins, magical node, ley lines or a magical past put an older town's ruins beneath; mines and mountains make caverns likelier; catacombs only under cemeteries, never under churches, only from a town upward; the cathedral always has the largest crypt; a cemetery the record closes stops its catacomb growing; nothing lost below.

Plain words: in a city (10 000 people or more) whose record lists its water system the map may carry an aqueduct on arches from a spring or river in reach to the city's conduit house, and a raised road may link a citadel, palace or cathedral on high ground; a town gets these only if the DM draws them; they are the map's own additions, removable by the DM and staying removed through later updates; the history panel says why each was built; a toll bridge gets a stream to cross, never a bridge over dry land.

Plain words: DM sees and edits everything, co-DM edits too; players never receive the DM's map file or SF's record: their Map tab shows pictures of the town as the party knows it (unlearned place drawn but not named), redrawn after every DM save and reveal ('Reveal to the party'; 'See what the players see' switch); gallery and public pictures show only public names, SF-veiled words veiled; SF's AI assistant reads the map, answers 'where is the tannery and why', proposes changes as ghosts the DM accepts or drops; a player's assistant reads only the party's known places.

Plain words: the map program runs in its own frame on its own web address (as SF's realm map does), none of its code beside SF's accounts or payments; each map stored by SF next to its settlement, never inside the dossier, as a saved file plus the list of changes since, 'with two older copies kept as backups'. An unreadable dossier, an unknown SF version, or a settlement shrunk below the town floor never breaks the map: it shows the last good town with a plain note ('This map is held as it was. The settlement's record could not be read.'), loses nothing, catches up when a readable dossier arrives; 'A settlement under 1 500 people waits for the village product, which will plug into the same doorway; when it exists, a town that shrinks into a village, or a village that grows into a town, keeps one map.' Map tab: saved picture at once, live map within about a second for a town and two for a large city; player's tab opens the party's pictures at once; nothing asks the DM to fill in a form; nothing in SF has to change to make a map.

Map record: the host is the store (§11.3); for SF one map record per settlement map in its own row keyed by settlement id and map id, never inside the dossier's data blob (would ride every save, sync and public projection at about ten times the dossier's size; research/sf/dossier-seam.md C-6; J-V8.3); type published by @plat/bridge-client as the host's storage contract; module never touches storage. The host never computes anything it stores (C8-04): every encoded event, head, sequence number and snapshot field arrives in a message; the host compares only strings it was handed (a proposal's baseLogHead against the logHead it holds; J-V8.46).

MapRecord (@plat/bridge-client; hashes lower-case hex): mapId (UUID the HOST mints when it first asks for a map = the document's docId, BCR-V8-2; immutable); settlementKey 'settlement:<id>' (§7.7 item 12; immutable); snapshot: SnapshotBlock (from dossier.result.created or doc.snapshot.ready, never computed by the host); tail {seq, event: Uint8Array as handed}[] (committed events after the snapshot, seq order); logHead (snapshot's when tail empty, else the last logHeadAfter accepted); adapter {line, version}; lastOffer {dossierHash, at ISO 8601, result: OfferStatus}; absorbed {factHash, week or null, dossierHash}; status current/stale/held/refreshing; held? {code: PortRefusalCode, message (English, logs), sinceDossierHash, reason {key, args?} (a host.held.* row; SS-44)}; refreshing? {by: page session holding the lease, until: now + 60 s renewed after each map} (C8-30); thumbnails {public?, secret?} PNG 512 px long side; party: PartyKnowledge (only setParty writes); partyPictures?: PartyPictureSet (only putPartyPictures writes); backups {bytes, logHead, docId (= mapId; restore refuses any other), at, tailAfter? (backups[0] only: tail segment the compaction removed, kept until next compaction, C8-27)}[] 'the two previous snapshots, newest first'; refreshPending; sizes {snapshot, tail, backups, thumbnails, party} bytes for the host's quota.

SnapshotBlock {bytes (.plat as §2.9 writes it), logHead (§11.3), lastSeq, outputVersion, schemaVersion, documentDigest (§2.9 digest over canonical bytes)}. PartyKnowledge {tier 'public' or 'local' (party's base key §9.2; never 'secret'), places: binding keys (inst:, quarter:, npc:) or a map place's address revealed above the tier, rev (+1 at every setParty), prev? {tier, places, rev} (state before the last setParty; 'Hide again' restores it), by? OfferStatus created/absorbed/unchanged/held/refused. PortRefusalCode E_RUNG_UNAVAILABLE, E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE, E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED, E_OTHER_SETTLEMENT.

MapRecord.status semantics: current = lastOffer.dossierHash equals the dossier the host holds and the result committed; stale = host holds a newer dossier than lastOffer; refreshing = a live refresh lease (refreshing.until in the future; an expired lease is free and status reads stale); held = last offer refused, held says why (§3.9). Written only through the client's store calls (§3.7, §3.14), each a compare-and-set conditioned on the logHead the host holds (or party.rev for the party), so two writers never interleave; party starts {tier public, places [], rev 0} at create.

Embed (1) SF's side: the Map tab is a lazy chunk imported by nothing eager (SF's first paint unchanged; C-10, E-8), holding SF's mount component and @plat/bridge-client (<= 12 KB gzipped with the party viewer, §6); a player's tab (audience player) calls mountParty: reads the record's partyPictures into the client's small pan-and-zoom viewer, no frame, module or message (§3.14; C8-01); the DM's and co-DM's tab calls mount: reads the map record, draws the viewer key's thumbnail at once as a static image if one exists (J-V8.24), creates one iframe src = moduleOrigin + embedPath + '#p=2', sandbox 'allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-downloads' (no top navigation, pop-ups or forms), allow '', referrerpolicy no-referrer, sized to the tab (J-V8.7); SF's CSP adds the module origin to frame-src; allow-same-origin is the module's OWN origin (workers and cache), granting nothing on SF's origin; mount refuses any audience word other than dm and co-dm before a frame exists. (2) Module's side: the module origin serves static files only: embed.html (second entry point of @plat/app, host mode: no file operations (fileMenu false), no DocResolver, bridge-driven; BCR-V8-3), lazily loaded chunks of the current output version and the retained N−1 and N−2 (§6.4), fonts, the stamp-tile asset; headers: Content-Security-Policy default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; worker-src 'self' blob:; img-src 'self' data: blob:; connect-src 'self' <the clerk origins>; frame-ancestors <SF's app origins>, where the clerk origins are a deployment row by V10's configuration (V10 §3.17): none under C ('SettlementForge's own assistant, the default recommended here') and under off; the proxy's origin (one of SF's app origins on the embed's allowlist) under B; the provider's API origin under A; no cross-origin isolation headers (§11.2); Cache-Control immutable on hashed chunks; the module holds no account, cookie or secret, trusts only messages whose origin is on its allowlist and whose source is its parent window (§11.3).

Embed (3) Boot: embed.html binds WindowPostMessageTransport to window.parent with the allowlist, sends module.status {booting}, starts the generation worker, the derivation pool (up to three workers, §4.1) and the tile worker, loads model packages of the current output version, sends ready {outputVersions, schemaVersion, protocol 2, adapters [{line, version}]} (BCR-V8-1); client flushes queued messages in order (§11.3); ready within bootTimeoutMs (20 s) or the client re-creates the frame once; a second miss leaves the thumbnail with the note 'the map could not start' and a retry button (§3.9 B1). (4) Load: client sends doc.load {bytes: snapshot, role, session, audience} (module re-derives role and key from audience by §14's table, takes the lower; J-V8.29) then doc.apply {baseLogHead: snapshot.logHead, events: tail}; module opens the snapshot (§2.9 steps 1-5: frozen view outside the window, corrupt cache replayed, verification in background), folds the tail, draws; first live frame replaces the thumbnail; an older snapshot.outputVersion inside the window replays exactly under its own version and module.status {upgrade-available} goes to an owner's client only (§3.8). (5) Offer: client decides whether to offer (§3.2) and commits the result (§3.3). (6) Switching settlements: MapSession.switchTo(spec) (same fields as mount; C8-40) reuses the frame: close on the handle, then load and offer the next record; boot paid once per page (J-V8.30); one document live per frame; previous one's memory released before the next is opened (§12.8 per document).

Embed (7) Bridge to the shell (SR-03; V9 XV-V9-17; J-V9.81): the bridge handler (V08's glue in embed.html, the one piece of host-mode code between transport and @plat/app's shell) fills the shell's two host surfaces and is their one channel to the bridge. X12); exportFormats (by §5.4 (2): every format §11.1's key rules admit for the frame's role and key, saved to the user's device); fileMenu false; historyFilter unset (only owner and editor frames at secret); J-V8.110); list with an uncached key returns only place-less lines (host.partyTier, host.picturesDrawn), starts reads, fires onChange on answer (J-V8.109); no key subscription of its own (the shell re-lists on onEffectiveKey, V9 §4.10); one line host.picturesDrawn 'Party pictures last drawn {time}' from partyPicturesAt; list starts empty at each doc.load (first party value is the baseline), never persisted (J-V8.58; J-V8.93)); newDocuments 'download' (V9 §3.9 host-mode rule; a copy of a dossier-bound document is detached, V6 §4.4; J-V8.93). (c) host.state: handler keeps the latest party, backups, partyPicturesAt in session memory; playersView and the header's toggle set ViewOpts.viewAs via setViewOpts (BCR-V9-23) through view.set (§11.3), clear with viewAs undefined. (d) Selection: reveal and hide carry the frame's current selection (entity ids forwarded in entity.selected, §5.4 (4)) as binding key when dossier-bound (Identity.dossier), else address. The handler lives as long as the frame and survives switchTo; host.state memory replaced after the next doc.load, historyLines cleared, players' view switched off at every load.

Offer decision and coalescing: the host cannot compute the fact hash, so it compares raw dossiers: hashDossier = SHA-256 (Web Crypto) of canonical JSON (keys sorted by code point, no insignificant whitespace, numbers as JavaScript prints them), lower-case hex; the DM's or co-DM's client offers when hashDossier(dossier) != record.lastOffer.dossierHash or when the record is held (every new dossier is a retry), never otherwise; a player's page never offers; the port decides at the fact level (J-V8.4): differences only outside the carried facts (generation log, prose, simulationTrace, never-read keys) return unchanged and the host stores the new lastOffer with nothing appended (T-V8-6). Coalescing (J-V8.23): at most one offer in flight per session; a newer dossier replaces any queued one; when the in-flight result returns the newest is offered against the new head; the client counts skipped versions in its report field coalesced (client-side; no port note; C8-34); skipped versions lose nothing (the port diffs carried facts against the newest; each change's week from receipts, §4.11 (2)); an element appearing and vanishing between offers is never seen (same answer as SF's end-state).

Port leader: the port runs inside the module (generation worker, beside the document), never in SF's bundle (J-V8.1); only an editing role (DM owner or co-DM editor) holds the document, dossier and a port; a player holds neither (C8-01; J-V8.2 revised); digest, creation, absorb are pure functions of (document, dossier, HostContext, adapter and table versions), so every editing client computes the same events; every port event carries reserved session host:port (C8-15; BCR-V8-19) so events are byte-identical whichever editor computed them (T-V8-3) and no user's undo stack holds one. Creation (no map record): host mints mapId, sends dossier.offer {create {mapId}}; module runs digest -> creation (§14: blueprint, creation prefix, binding, carried facts) -> generate(blueprint, {docId: mapId, prefix}) (BCR-V8-2; J-V8.13); replies dossier.result {created, created: SnapshotBlock, factHash, report} (.plat bytes with logHead, lastSeq, outputVersion, schemaVersion, documentDigest computed by the module; C8-04); host calls MapStore.create as handed ('exists' -> another client won; reload the stored record, byte-identical by determinism, T-V8-3), writes the two thumbnails and renders the first party picture set. Absorb (a record exists): digest -> absorb(doc, digest, host) (§14; steps §3.5-§3.6), dry-run on the working state (§7.1; never refused by map locks or pins, applied around them, §7.7 items 2, 5), replies dossier.result {absorbed, baseLogHead, events, encoded, seqAfter, logHeadAfter, factHash, week, report} WITHOUT folding; host treats it as a doc.changed: if baseLogHead is current it commits (MapStore.commitEvents), sets its head to logHeadAfter, fans doc.apply out to every open session incl. the sender (which folds; §11.3 convergence); else doc.rejected {stale} and the module re-runs absorb on the new head (bounded: three attempts, then module.status {error} and a retry at the next offer). Verification by every editor (C8-37): an editing client folding a doc.apply with host:port events and holding the same dossier (last offer's hash equals the result's dossierHash) re-runs absorb on the pre-apply state and compares encodings; a difference is a port mismatch (module.status {error, detail host.verify.mismatch}, §3.9 B20, a report line naming the first differing event); never blocks the fold (T-V8-8). Two editors at once: both compute the same events; the host accepts the first, answers the second stale; the second's re-run finds nothing left (unchanged); no election protocol; the log's single head is the arbiter (J-V8.2).

Refresh queue (J-V8.6): after SF commits an advance, the host marks refreshPending on every map record whose dossier changed (hashDossier) and calls MapHost.refresh(queue) from the DM's page; the client creates ONE hidden frame (embed.html#p=2&mode=refresh: no tile worker, no view, no thumbnail pass until the end) processing the queue serially in campaign order, one document at a time: take the record's refresh lease (setStatus refreshing {by session, until now + 60 s}; refused when another live lease holds it; C8-30) -> doc.load + tail -> dossier.offer -> commit -> compact if the tail exceeds its threshold (§3.7) -> render the two thumbnails and party picture set (tile worker started for this step only) -> release lease with status current and refreshPending cleared -> close document, release memory -> next; lease renewed after each step, expires on its own (a dead page's lease expires within 60 s; record reads stale meanwhile). Scheduling: runs while the DM is not interacting with a map frame (paused on pointer or key input in any visible map session, resumes 5 s after the last), yields between maps, stops on AbortSignal. Page memory (C8-23): the refresh frame does not start while a visible map frame holds a CITY or METROPOLIS document; runs when the Map tab is closed or the visible document is a TOWN (at most one CITY or METROPOLIS document per page; §6 page row); queue persisted by refreshPending (next page resumes); a map opened in a visible tab while queued is absorbed there first and dropped from the queue; serial keeps memory at one rung's line (§12.8) plus the frame's fixed cost (a campaign of 20 CITY maps after a year in about 1.5 minutes of background work incl. party sets, §6).

digest(raw, host) steps (§14 item 2's duties; all pure): (1) adapter: AdapterRegistry.select(raw, {line: host.line, bound}); refusal ends (E_LINE_UNSUPPORTED); (2) limits: a bounded walk measures bytes of keys and strings, depth, list lengths against the manifest's limits; over any -> E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE with a size_limit note naming the first limit (T-V8-20); no string longer than maxString copied; (3) shape: every requiredKeys key present with the types read (id 's_' + 16 hex, name non-empty string, tier a string, population an integer in [0, 1e7] (0 a deserted settlement routed by §3.6 (7); SS-21), institutions an array, _seed present); failure -> E_UNKNOWN_SHAPE listing up to 20 violations; an extra top-level key never a failure (C8-03): read-false optional or unnamed key dropped into ignored with ignored_key; the hand-made teaching file fails here (§14); (4) records: each institution, power, notable, condition, calamity checked for required fields (a name; an institution a category string; numbers finite); a failing record QUARANTINED (kept out of the digest, its key when formable listed in DossierBinding.quarantined with the reason, quarantined_record note), the rest proceeds (J-V8.8; §3.9 B4); the diff never removes a quarantined key; a quarantine whose key cannot be formed holds every absent institution key (C8-12).

digest step (5) keys, grammar, class: name grammar and ladder step (§3.5.1); §7.7 item 12's key law with housing records set aside for DR7 by their @housing row; CLASS LOOKUP CHAIN (DR24): (a) renamedFrom -> kinds row of the slug of its CURRENT name; (b) else its kind (catalogue key) -> its kinds row; (c) else the slug of its name as a catalogue key; (d) else the tags rung (C8-33): tags mapping through tags to exactly one family whose generic class exists -> that class, noted unmapped_kind with rung tags; (e) else its category's generic class, noted unmapped_kind — for (d), (e) the note written after the fold, its class the class building the record at the document's rung (§4.6; §3.6 (4); at a village rung V07 §3.11 step 4's tag fallback; SR4-07); (f) a CUSTOM record's class and profile NOT decided at digest (SS-12; J-VI.20): (b)-(e) do not run; the digest carries inputs (custom scene tokens, group, keyword keys; tags; category; admitted custom-def fact) and item 104 (a)'s resolution with V11 §3.13.1's rungs (author's map declaration for its localUid, archetype, category, tags, definition fields, keywords with their class cell, then generic-other) decides at fold; custom_resolved written after that fold naming the deciding rung; a pseudo-class kinds row routes the record to its reader with no roster class (@absent to S2, SS-10); a catalogue record's siting-profile family = kinds row family when set, else tags families (item 103 (a); combination rule in §10.2), else its generic class's own; political role carried as given (DR12, J-V8.45).

digest step (6) powers, notables, circumstances, economy: standings = power / sum power rounded to 1/10 000; controlled list via the line's stable part (§7.7 item 12); relations from powerStructure.factionRelationships one per unordered pair with type and direction words (relations row at the put); notables' workplace and power resolved by name (absent, noted name_unjoined); deposits; every listed condition whatever its status; stressors normalised (stressors, else stress, one object or list: each {type} a condition cond:stress:<type>, source stressor, severity 0.5, no weeks; C8-09); quarters; government and security; economy: each activeChains[] into economy.chains (resource joined to a listed deposit by resourceKey, processors by the name rule, outputs via goodWords, upstreamChains as chain:cat: keys, status via chainStatus; C8-06); tradeDependencies into economy.dependencies (institution by name, severity via dependencySeverity); primaryExports, primaryImports with necessityImports, transit into economy.goods via goodWords; calamities keyed calamity:<tick>:<slug(name)>, severity by calamitySeverity over deaths and population at its week (latest populationHistory at or before, else current), targets by name (C8-09); sea threats by threats row; ruin evidence by ruinEvidence row; latitude by DR-V8.1; never-read keys dropped into ignored (§7.7 item 1); severities round to 1/1 000 and percentages to 1/100 (J-V8.17). Name resolution (chain processors, dependency institutions, calamity targets; C8-06 (3)): exact name -> key; else KIND FAMILY (names with count range and qualifiers removed, case-folded, last word's plural folded to singular: -ies -> -y, -es after s, x, z, ch, sh, else final -s) -> the one record of that family (several: first in dossier order, noted name_ambiguous); else unjoined, kept by name, noted chain_node_unjoined (research mapping row 46: 2 585 of 3 381 processor names join exactly; kind family measured by T-V8-34); goods words by V11 §3.13.5 matching; no match noted unmapped_good (SR1-26). (7) custom content: §3.13's steps. (8) ladder merges: §3.5.1 (c). (9) seed: settlement.seed = H32('plat:sf-seed' || _seed) (§14 item 2); _seed and _config go no further.

The diff (absorb's first step): carried facts vs the new digest under the same keys, key by key in code-point order, skipping every quarantined key (C8-12; a quarantine without a formable key holds every carried institution key absent from the new digest, one quarantine_hold note). Per kind (key only new / only carried / fields compared -> op): settlement: —; — (a different settlement key refuses, E_OTHER_SETTLEMENT); population -> population; tierWord -> tier (F8); name -> rename (title only). institution: add (F1); under a key carried as removed or ruined -> reopen (F6); a greater whose lesser is carried -> add, the lesser's members re-bound as the greater's where the greater's thing is the lesser's, else the greater placed new and the lesser's key bound as at a first reading (§3.5.1 (c), (d); SR5-01) / remove with fate vanished (SF never deletes, research V48) unless a ladder promotion re-binds it or a quarantine holds it / state, fate, inactive -> state (F2, F3, F5 by item 14, fates first); Chains' links (item 105 (i); DR-V8.5; C8-06): SF's chains become links of item 105's supply web between bound members, DERIVED at every placement and epoch by the base web (item 105 (a): never stored) from carried chain and dependency facts; the port stores only facts. Name grammar (the base's T9 extended, BCR-V8-5; in order): (1) (lo-hi+) -> count [lo, hi], openTop true (members may exceed hi up to V11's per-kind-and-rung cap, reported; Parish churches (50-100+)); (2) (lo-hi) -> count [lo, hi] (Taverns (5-20)); (3) (n+ only) -> popQualifier n (a population floor kept in the label, never a count; Cathedral (10,000+ only)); (4) every other parenthesised group -> its case-folded words appended to qualifiers ((guild), (red light district), (divine, 1st level)); digits may carry thousands separators; kindLabel = name with groups 1 and 2 removed and trimmed; a housing-stock record is told by its @housing kinds row, not the grammar.

Step type: V11's dossier.ladders row for the record's kind (catalogId, else name slug) gives step and lesser; with no row the qualifiers row over the record's qualifiers in order (first with a step); none with a count range -> COUNT; else no step. An unnumbered COUNT, QUARTER or GUILD record takes V11's range column (range at the kind's lowest tier) x its rungScale only at rungs above that tier (V11 §3.12); at a village rung (THORP, HAMLET, VILLAGE) an unnumbered record takes V07 §2.4's range row for its step type and member class (village.json rules.ladders.ranges keyed by step type with the qualifier as label; V07 SR1-16, J-V7.105), else V11's range unscaled (SS-08); a kind whose qualifier names a step V11's table lacks is noted ladder_unknown; a record whose kind is a greater of the committed ladderPairs the catalogue does not list is read as a plain record, noted uncatalogued_step (V11 §3.12).

No double counting (item 108 (c)): where a greater and a lesser of one ladder row are both in the dossier, the lesser gets mergedInto = the greater's key: not placed on its own, its range not added, the roster's per-capita members of that class ARE the greater's members, its binding key an alias row on the greater's member #1 (SIZE and REPLACEMENT: the greater's building — save a pin-record lesser, which V11 §3.12's row keeps as a pin of the greater's plot: parish_church over wayside_shrine binds the shrine's key to the churchyard cross, laid by V07 §3.10's pin-record rule at a village rung (VS8 at generation, village.records at an epoch or absorb; V07 §2.4, §3.10, §3.12 item 4; SR4-01, SR5-01), while at a base rung (no churchyard cross laid) it aliases the church building; the target chosen where the merge is first read — creation, or the absorb or epoch bringing the pair — and kept across a later rung change (§3.10; SR4-06; J-V8.111)), noted ladder_merged. A pair meeting over time (SR5-01; J-V8.113), lesser already placed and greater arriving beside it: (1) greater's thing is the lesser's (every COUNT, QUARTER, GUILD, SIZE, and REPLACEMENT rows keeping the lesser's thing: graveyard over burial_ground (face re-bound), wizard_s_tower over hedge_wizard (house becomes the tower), mages_guild over wizard_s_tower (tower binds the guild's hall), professional_city_watch over town_watch (posts carry on), cathedral_10_000_only over parish_church (church converted in place with its crypt, V6 §3.9.11)): lesser's placed members re-bound as the greater's #1..#n (nearest its demand first; a rebind each, no address change), DR9 adds members up to the greater's count by least disruption, nothing closes; (2) a lesser with no thing of its own (@none or @office: citizen_militia, traveling_performers, traveling_hedge_wizard, gates_if_walled, priest_resident): greater placed as any added record, lesser's key an alias row on member #1; (3) every other REPLACEMENT greater is a new thing placed new in the absorb or epoch bringing it (a building by DR9, an assign of its member (§3.6 (5)), at a village rung via V07's records placement item 4; a @wall greater by the fortification's dossier path (DR2 walls; V6 §3.7.6 (4); at a village rung V07 §3.11's palisade REPLACEMENT)), the lesser's key binding as at a first reading, its row re-pointed by one rebind (fold re-points, §3.6 (5)), noted ladder_merged (ladder_promoted under (d)): (i) a building lesser (fish_market over fishmonger): alias row on the greater's building (village: rim hall, V07 §3.12 (b)), the shop keeping its use unbound; (ii) a pin-record lesser: at a village rung the churchyard cross laid in that batch after the church, at a base rung an alias row on the church, the lesser's former pin standing unbound (a pin lesser whose row keeps no pin — wayside_shrine under cathedral_10_000_only — takes an alias row on the greater's building); (iii) a @wall lesser (town_walls over palisade or palisade_or_earthworks and the wall rows above): alias row on the enceinte the fortification path yields; the superseded ring keeps no binding.

Guild halls (V11 §3.12; SS-23; J-V8.83): a GUILD record's hall binds as one member #k of a craft_guilds_* COUNT record (categories family craft) or merchant_guilds_* COUNT record (family trade) in the same dossier, noted ladder_merged: the GUILD records of that family take members #1..#m in dossier order; the COUNT record's placed count = max(DR9's draw, m), above its range's top only when the GUILD records alone exceed it (noted count_over_range); no further hall; at an absorb a hall already placed is re-bound as #k (rebind, no address change), never duplicated; a COUNT record leaving the list releases its bound halls back to their GUILD records (a rebind each), so no hall closes by a change of wording; a GUILD record of another family, or with no such COUNT record, keeps its own hall; fixtures' cases: the three metropolises' two church ranges and metropolis-3's two cathedral records (§2.6a (3)).

Steps over time (item 108 (d)): a promotedFrom receipt (upgraded_by_reconstruction) keeps the record's one key (§7.7 item 12's F15 re-binding; the line keeps the old kind's catalogId); greater's thing is the lesser's ((c) first case): re-keys the singular record's binding row to the greater's #1 (rebind), DR9 adds the rest inside the new range by least disruption; greater a new thing ((c) third case; SR5-01; J-V8.114): placed new under the record's key (village: V07 §3.12 item 4) and the binding row re-pointed from the lesser's former thing to it (rebind); one key binds one thing (J-V8.111), the former thing left standing unbound (fishmonger's shop keeps its use; roadside shrine standing; a palisade the new ring superseded decaying by its persistence rows); a pin the row keeps (churchyard cross of parish_church over wayside_shrine at a village rung) laid in that batch by V07 §3.10's pin-record rule for the record, keyed by its binding key and provenance the record, with no binding row of its own; a lesser leaving the list in the same absorb that adds its greater with no receipt is read the same way (promotion, ladder_promoted, never removal plus addition). A demotedFrom receipt (demoted_by_disaster) keeps the member nearest its demand as the singular record (re-bound) and closes the rest by the receipt's fate (F2; a calamity's ruins stand as ruins); a burial record's demotion or promotion follows the same rules (no burial face closes by wording; §2.6a (4)). Custom content (item 108 (e)): a custom record whose admitted library entry lists subsumes is SIZE when the subsumed kinds belong to another V11 family, GUILD when a craft of its own family, SIZE when unknown; its lesser = subsumed kinds, merged by (c).

Re-check against the ladder file (CONFIRMED; C8-07 (2)): SF's ladder data at the pinned commit (src/data/institutionLadders.js at 5d699cc68, blob 91f6e2bd..., read as data, nothing copied) compared with V11 §3.12's rows: agreements (every row V11 marks ladder or subsumption); rows V11 marked inferred that the file holds (craft_guilds_100_150, merchant_guilds_50_100, banking_houses, banking_district with pawnbroker, gambling_halls, gambling_district, multiple_criminal_factions, multiple_adventurers_guilds with hireling_hall, slave_market_district, carriers_guild, cartographer_s_guild, large_prison, mages_district with mages_guild, alchemist_shop, alchemist_quarter, thieves_guild_powerful with black_market_bazaar and contract_killer, mint_official with assay_office, international_trade_center over caravan_masters_exchange and caravaneer_s_post); disagreements (hospital_network's lessers are almshouse and foundling_home; dungeon_delving_supply_district's lesser is bowyers_fletchers_guild); pairs the file holds that V11 lacked (wayside shrine -> parish church; water source -> multiple water sources; traveling performers -> theaters; hedge wizard and traveling hedge wizard -> wizard's tower; wizard's tower -> mages' guild; carriers' guild -> caravan masters' exchange; academy of magic, assassins' guild, auction house, gladiatorial school, printing house, great library, major port, specialized metalworkers, caravaneer's post, chroniclers' exchange, whisper market, black market, thieves' guild chapter over their named lessers; major hospital over almshouse); rows V11 infers that the file lacks (parish_churches_50_100, multiple_monasteries, major_monasteries_5_10, great_cathedral, burial_grounds_and_charnel_house, ...) stay inferred (dossiers list both forms); every fix a table change handed to revise-V11 (X1), reported by R2 when a baseline moves.
